If, however, someone were to maintain: 'Perception apprehends only the positive aspect, since it arises through the sense-organ door, and the sense-organ's activity is only in the positive aspect; but the cognition of non-existence emerges as a mental cognition, independent of sense-organ activity, after the cognition of the real entity and when the memory of the counter-correlate is present' — as stated:
"For this cognition 'it does not exist' is not produced by the sense-organ,

children.text: bhāvâṃśenâiva saṃyogo yogyatvād indriyasya hi" // NAV_1.15:1 //
children.translated_text: since the sense-organ's connection is only with the positive aspect, due to its capacity being thus,"
"Having grasped the existence of the real entity and having remembered the counter-correlate,
the mental cognition of non-existence arises independently of the sense-organ."

children.text: atrôcyate bhāvâṃśād abhāvâṃśas tarhy abhinno bhinno vā? abhinnaś cet, katham agrahaṇam, bhāvâṃśād avyatiriktatvād eva, tat-svarūpavat. bhinnaś ced, ghaṭâdy-abhāva-vinirluṭhitaṃ bhū-talam ādya-darśanena gṛhyata iti ghaṭâdayo gṛhyanta iti prāptaṃ, tad-abhāvâgrahaṇasya tad-bhāva-grahaṇanântarīyakatvāt. tathā câbhāvo 'pi paścāt pravartamānas tān utsārayitum apaṭiṣṭhaḥ syād, anyathā pratyakṣam asaṅkīrṇasya saṅkīrṇatā-grahaṇād bhrāntam āpanīpadyeta. kiṃ ca, pramāṇâbhāvād arthâbhāvo 'bhāva-pramāṇena sādhyata iti bhavato 'bhiprāyaḥ:
children.translated_text: To this we reply: Is the negative aspect, then, identical with or different from the positive aspect? If identical, how can it not be grasped, since it is not distinct from the positive aspect, just like the intrinsic nature of that very thing? If different, then since the ground-surface divested of the absence of a pot and the like is grasped by the initial perception, it would follow that pots and the like are grasped — because the non-grasping of their absence is inseparable from the grasping of their existence. Moreover, the absence, operating subsequently, would be unable to remove them; otherwise perception would turn out to be erroneous, since it would grasp the unmixed as mixed. Furthermore, your intended meaning is that the absence of an object is established by the <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence) from the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> [for it]:
"Where the five <s>pramāṇas</s> do not arise with respect to the nature of a real entity,
there the <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence) serves the purpose of cognizing the existence of that entity."

children.text: iti-vacanāt, tad ayuktam, yataḥ pramāṇâbhāvaḥ kathaṃ grāhyaḥ? tad-grāhaka-pramāṇântarâbhāvād iti cet, tasyâpy abhāva-grahaṇe tad-grāhaka-pramāṇântarâbhāvo grāhya ity anavasthā. atha arthâbhāvāt pramāṇasya pramāṇâbhāvāc cârthasyâbhāvaḥ pratipadyeta iti manyethās, tad etad itarêtarâśrayaṃ durghaṭam āpadyeta: na yāvad arthâbhāvo 'gṛhītas tāvat pramāṇâbhāvaḥ sidhyaty, arthâbhāvaś ca pramāṇâbhāvāt setsyatîty āvartanāt. athêndriyavat svayam avijñāto 'pi pramāṇâbhāvo 'rthâbhāvaṃ jñāpayiṣyatîty abhidadhīthās, tad ayuktam, tasya tucchatayā sakala-śakti-viraha-lakṣaṇatvād, indriyasya tu tad-viparyastatayā jñānôtpādana-dakṣatvāt. tasmāt pratyakṣam evam bhū-talâdi-pratiniyata-vastu-grāhitāṃ bibharti, yadi tad-viparīta-ghaṭâdi-pratiyogi-vastv-antara-vaiviktyaṃ tasyâkalayati nânyathā, vijātīya-vyavacchedâbhāve tasyâiva pratiniyatatvâsiddheḥ, sakala-saṅkīrṇatayā grahaṇa-prasaṅgāt. ato 'dhika-grāhyâbhāvān nirviṣayatayâbhāvâkhyaṃ pramāṇaṃ yat paraiḥ paryakalpi tad apramāṇam iti sthitam.
children.translated_text: Thus stated, this is improper, because: How is the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> to be grasped? If you say, 'from the absence of another <s>pramāṇa</s> that would grasp it,' then for grasping the absence of that one too, the absence of yet another <s>pramāṇa</s> that would grasp it must be grasped — and so there is an infinite regress. If you should think that from the absence of the object the absence of the <s>pramāṇa</s> is understood, and from the absence of the <s>pramāṇa</s> the absence of the object is understood — that would incur the fault of mutual dependence, which is untenable: for as long as the absence of the object is not grasped, the absence of the <s>pramāṇa</s> cannot be established, and the absence of the object is to be established from the absence of the <s>pramāṇa</s> — thus there is circularity. If you should maintain that the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s>, though itself unknown, would make known the absence of an object — just as the sense-organ does [with objects] — that is improper, because that [absence] being empty is characterized by the complete absence of all powers, whereas the sense-organ, being the opposite of that, is capable of producing knowledge. Therefore, perception itself bears the capacity to grasp entities determined to a particular locus such as the ground-surface; and if it apprehends the distinctness of other counter-correlative entities such as pots and the like that are contrary to it — then and only then, not otherwise — since without exclusion of the dissimilar, the determination of that very entity to a particular locus cannot be established, as there would be the absurd consequence of grasping everything as mixed up. Therefore, because there is no additional object to be grasped, the <s>pramāṇa</s> called <s>abhāva</s> that was postulated by others, being without an object, is established as not a valid <s>pramāṇa</s>.
by showing the definite twofold nature,

children.text: -parikalpitaṃ ‘pratyakṣam anumānaṃ cêti'; dvaividhyam apakṣipati, tad-ākūtena tasyâyogāt. pratyakṣâtiriktaṃ hi tādātmya-tad-utpatti-lakṣaṇa-sambandhôpalakṣita-kārya-svabhāvânupalabdhi-rūpa-liṅga-traya-sampādita-janmakam anumānam eva pramāṇaṃ, na śābdôhâdikaṃ, sambandha-vikalatvād iti tad-ākūtam. ayuktaṃ câitat, pratyakṣânumānâtirikta-pramāṇântarâbhāva-grahaṇôpāyâbhāvāt. na tāvat pratyakṣāt pramāṇântarâbhāvâvagatis, tasya svalakṣaṇa-viṣayatvenâbhāva-grāhitā-virodhāt. nâpi svabhāva-kāryânumānābhyāṃ, tayor vastu-sādhakatvāt. nâpy anupalabdhes, tasyā apy atyantâbhāva-sādhana-virodhāt. sā hi catur-vidhā varṇyate mūla-bhedâpekṣayā, tad yathā -- viruddhôpalabdhir viruddha-kāryôpalabdhiḥ kāraṇânupalabdhiḥ svabhāvânupalabdhiś cêti. na tāvad viruddhôpalabdheḥ pramāṇântarasyâtyantâbhāvo, dṛśyâtmano viruddhasya vidhānenêtarâbhāva-sādhanāt, sannihita-deśa eva pratiyogy-abhāva-siddheḥ. etena viruddha-kāryôpalabdhir api vyākhyātā, tasyā api pratiṣedhya-virodhi-sannidhāpana-dvāreṇâbhāva-sādhakatvāt. kāraṇânupalabdhir api tad-deśâśaṅkita-kāryasyâivâbhāvaṃ sādhayati na sarvatra, svayam asiddhatvāt. svabhāvânupalabdhir apy eka-jñāna-saṃsargi-padârthôpalambha-rūpā tad-deśa eva pratidvandvy-abhāvaṃ gamayati. ataḥ pramāṇântarasyâpi kvacin niṣedhaḥ syān, na sarvatra. tan na pramāṇântara-bādhakaṃ samasti.
children.translated_text: postulated twofold division '<s>pratyakṣa</s> and <s>anumāna</s>' is rejected, since it does not accord with the purport thereof. For the <s>pramāṇa</s> beyond <s>pratyakṣa</s> is only <s>anumāna</s>, which is born from the three types of logical marks — <s>kārya</s> (effect), <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature), and <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) — characterized by the relation of essential identity and causal origination; and not <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony), <s>ūha</s> (reasoning), and the like, since they lack the [required] relation — such is their purport. But this is improper, because there is no means of grasping the absence of any <s>pramāṇa</s> other than <s>pratyakṣa</s> and <s>anumāna</s>. Firstly, not from <s>pratyakṣa</s> can the absence of another <s>pramāṇa</s> be cognized, since its being restricted to <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (unique particulars) as its object is incompatible with the capacity to grasp absence. Nor from <s>svabhāva</s> or <s>kārya</s> inference, since both of these establish a positive entity. Nor from <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), since that too is incompatible with establishing absolute absence. For that is described as fourfold with respect to the basic divisions: namely, apprehension of the contradictory, apprehension of the effect of the contradictory, non-apprehension of the cause, and non-apprehension of the essential nature. Now, from the apprehension of the contradictory, the absolute absence of another <s>pramāṇa</s> does not follow, because it establishes the absence of one thing through the positive establishment of its contradictory, which is of a perceptible nature — thus only the absence of the counter-correlate in the proximate location is established. By this, the apprehension of the effect of the contradictory is also explained, since it too establishes absence through the door of bringing near the contradictory of what is to be negated. Non-apprehension of the cause also establishes only the absence of the effect suspected to be in that location, not everywhere, since it itself is not established [everywhere]. Non-apprehension of the essential nature too, being in the form of apprehending an entity conjoined with a single cognition, indicates the absence of the rival only in that location. Therefore, there might be negation of another <s>pramāṇa</s> somewhere, but not everywhere. Hence there is no means that can invalidate other <s>pramāṇas</s> universally.

children.text: pratyakṣânumānayoś ca prāmāṇyaṃ kuta iti cintyam. na tāvat pratyakṣāt, tasya nirvikalpakatayā sato 'py asat-kalpatvāt. tat-pṛṣṭha-bhāvī vikalpas tu na svalakṣaṇâmbhodhi-madhyam avagāhate; tat kathaṃ tatrâpraviṣṭas tat-svarūpaṃ niścinuyāt. apramāṇa-bhūtāc ca tasmāt prāmāṇya-nirṇaya iti nibiḍa-jaḍimâviṣkaraṇaṃ bhavatām. anumānāt prāmāṇya-nirṇaya iti cen, na, tasyâpi svalakṣaṇād bahiḥ plavanāt. aprāmāṇya-vyavacchedas tena sādhyata iti cen, na, vyavacchedasya vyavacchinnâvyatirekād, itarathândhakāra-nartana-kalpam anumānam āsajyeta, nirviṣayatvāt. kiṃ ca, tat-prāmāṇya-nirṇāyakam anumānaṃ pramāṇam apramāṇaṃ vā? na tāvad apramāṇam, tataḥ prāmāṇyâsiddheḥ. nâpi pramāṇaṃ, tat-prāmāṇya-sādhakâbhāvāt. na hi pratyakṣāt tat-siddhir, vikalpa-śūnyatayâkiñcit-karatvād ity uktam. anumānāt tu tat-sādhane vikalpa-yugalaṃ tad-avastham evâvatiṣṭheta, tat-prāmāṇya-sādhane 'py anumāna-kalpanêty anavasthā. kiṃ ca, gṛhīta-sambandhasyânumānaṃ pravarteta, sambandhas tri-kāla-gocaro grāhyo, na ca pratyakṣaṃ taṃ lakṣayituṃ kṣamate, pūrvâpara-kṣaṇa-truṭita-rūpa-vārtamānika-kṣaṇa-grahaṇa-paryavasita-sattākatvāt, tad-uttara-kāla-bhāvino vikalpasyâpi vyāvahārikâbhiprāyeṇa tan-niṣṭhatâbhyupagamāt. anumānād grahīṣyatîti cen nanu tad api sambandha-pūrvakaṃ pravarteta, tad-grahaṇe 'pîyaṃ vārtêty anavasthā. tasmād anumānam abhilaṣatā gaty-antarâbhāvāt tat-sambandha-grahaṇa-pravaṇas tri-kāla-gocaro 'vyabhicārī vitarko 'bhyupagantavyaḥ. tathā ca prastuta-tad-dvaividhyasya vighaṭitatvād, anyad api yad evaṃ-vidham avisaṃvādi jñānaṃ tat pramāṇam astv ity alaṃ śuṣkâbhimānenêti. yadi punaḥ sādhyârthânyathânupapanna-hetu-sampāditam anumānam iṣyeta, tadā pratyakṣam anumānaṃ cêty api dvaividhyaṃ ghaṭām aṭed eva; pratyakṣa-vyatirikta-jñānasya sāmastyenânumāne 'ntar-bhāva-sambhavāt, anyathânupapannârthântaram antareṇa parokṣârtha-viṣaya-pratīter abhāvād iti.
children.translated_text: And from what does the validity of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference) derive? — this must be considered. Not from <s>pratyakṣa</s>, for being non-conceptual, though real it is as good as non-existent. And the conceptual cognition that follows after it does not plunge into the ocean of <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (unique particulars); so how could it, not having entered therein, ascertain its true nature? And to say that the determination of validity comes from that which is not a valid <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is a display of dense stupidity on your part. If you say the determination of validity comes from <s>anumāna</s> — no, since that too floats outside of <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. If you say that the exclusion of invalidity is established by it — no, since the exclusion is not different from what is excluded; otherwise <s>anumāna</s> would be reduced to something like dancing in the dark, being without an object. Moreover, is the <s>anumāna</s> that determines its validity a <s>pramāṇa</s> or not? Not the latter, for then the validity would not be established. Nor the former, since there is no means of establishing its validity. For its establishment cannot come from <s>pratyakṣa</s>, which, being devoid of conceptual thought, is incapable of accomplishing anything — as stated. But if one attempts to establish it from <s>anumāna</s>, the pair of conceptual cognitions would remain in the same condition, and in establishing the validity of that too, the postulation of yet another <s>anumāna</s> leads to infinite regress. Furthermore, <s>anumāna</s> would operate for one who has grasped the relation, and the relation to be grasped extends over all three times; but <s>pratyakṣa</s> is not capable of perceiving it, since its existence is confined to grasping the present momentary form, severed from the earlier and later moments; and even the conceptual thought that follows after it is accepted as resting upon it only in a conventional sense. If you say it will be grasped from <s>anumāna</s> — but that too would operate on the basis of a prior relation, and in grasping that relation too, this same problem recurs — hence infinite regress. Therefore, one who desires <s>anumāna</s>, for lack of any other recourse, must accept a reasoning faculty (<s>vitarka</s>) that is inclined to grasp that relation, that extends over all three times, and that is unfailing. And since in that case the proposed twofold division is dismantled, whatever other such unfailing cognition there may be — let that too be a <s>pramāṇa</s> — enough with hollow pride! If, however, <s>anumāna</s> is accepted as that which is produced by a reason that is otherwise-inexplicable with respect to the object to be proved, then even the twofold division '<s>pratyakṣa</s> and <s>anumāna</s>' would be workable; because it is possible to include all knowledge other than <s>pratyakṣa</s> collectively under <s>anumāna</s>, since there is no cognition of an indirect object without recourse to something other that is otherwise inexplicable.
Now he states the reason for the established restriction by means of the very words of the <s>sūtra</s>:
from the determination of the objects of knowledge

children.text: ca kākâkṣi-golaka-nyāyenâtrâpi sambandhanīyam. tataś câyam artho: dvābhyām eva prakārābhyāṃ meyasya grāhyârthasya viniścayāt svarūpa-nirṇayād; dve eva yathôkte pramāṇe na nyūnam adhikaṃ cêti. ayam atrâbhiprāyaḥ: sva-saṃvedanaṃ prati nikhila-jñānānām eka-rūpatayā sākṣāt-karaṇa-caturatvān nâsty eva bhedaḥ; bahir-arthaṃ punar apekṣya kaścic cakṣurâdi-sāmagrī-bala-labdha-sattākaḥ svâvayava-vyāpinaṃ kālântara-saṃcariṣṇuṃ sthagita-kṣaṇa-vivartam alakṣita-paramâṇu-pārimāṇḍalyaṃ sannihitaṃ viśada-nirbhāsaṃ sāmānyam ākāraṃ sākṣāt-kurvāṇaḥ prakāśaḥ prathate, tatra pratyakṣa-vyavahāraḥ pravartate. yaḥ punar liṅga-śabdâdi-dvāreṇa niyatâniyata-sāmānyâkārâvalokī parisphuṭatā-rahitaḥ khalv ātmano 'rtha-grahaṇa-pariṇāmaḥ samullasati sa parokṣatāṃ svī-karoti. na câitau prakārau vihāya prakārântareṇa jñāna-pravṛttiṃ paśyāmo, na câpaśyantaḥ pramāṇântara-parikalpanaṃ kṣamāmahe, na ca dvayoḥ prathamānayor ekaṃ nihnuvānam apekṣāmahe, viśeṣâbhāvāt. tasmād etad eva dvaividhyam urarī-kartavyam iti sthitam.
children.translated_text: should also be connected here by the principle of the crow's-eye-ball (<s>kākākṣi-golaka-nyāya</s>). And so this is the meaning: because the knowable object (<s>meya</s>), i.e., the apprehensible object (<s>grāhyārtha</s>), is determined by only two modes — i.e., its own nature is ascertained [in two ways] — there are only two <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition) as stated, neither fewer nor more. The intention here is this: with respect to <s>sva-saṃvedana</s> (self-awareness), since all cognitions are of a single form and are skilled in direct apprehension, there is no distinction whatsoever. But with regard to external objects, a certain manifestation (<s>prakāśa</s>) — whose existence is obtained through the power of the assemblage of conditions such as the eye, etc. — which directly apprehends a general form (<s>sāmānya-ākāra</s>) that pervades its own parts, that will migrate to another time, that has its momentary transformations concealed, that has the atomic sphericity unnoticed, that is proximate, and that has a vivid appearance — that [manifestation] shines forth, and therein the usage '<s>pratyakṣa</s>' (perception) operates. But whatever apprehension-transformation of the self arises through the door of marks (<s>liṅga</s>), words (<s>śabda</s>), and the like — observing general forms that are both determined and undetermined, devoid of full clarity — that assumes the character of indirectness (<s>parokṣatā</s>). And we do not see the operation of cognition by any mode other than these two modes, and not seeing [any other mode], we do not countenance the postulation of another <s>pramāṇa</s>, nor do we look for the denial of one of these two that are [directly] experienced, since there is no distinguishing feature [to warrant it]. Therefore, it is established that precisely this twofold division must be accepted.

children.text: sāmprataṃ yad asmābhiḥ prāg vivṛṇvadbhir vyudapādi, yad uta vipratipannâvyutpanna-vyāmohâpoha-saham ihêdaṃ pramāṇa-lakṣaṇam iti tat-sūtra-mātra-darśanād eva vimala-buddhayo 'vagaccheyuḥ. manda-matayas tu tāvatā na bhotsyanta iti -- taddhita-vidhitsayā vyaktaṃ pramāṇa-lakṣaṇâbhidhāna-phalaṃ pratipipādayiṣur api sapūrva-pakṣaṃ nirākāṅkṣaṃ lakṣayeyus ta iti tāvat pūrva-pakṣam utthāpayann āha:
children.translated_text: Now, what was stated by us earlier in the course of explanation — namely, that this definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) is capable of removing the confusion of those who hold wrong views and of those who are unlearned — those of clear intellect would understand from seeing the <s>sūtra</s> (aphorism) alone. But those of dull understanding would not comprehend from that much alone — therefore, wishing to clearly demonstrate the result of stating the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>, together with the prior objection (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>), so that they might apprehend it without further inquiry, [the author] first raises the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (objection) and says:
The <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition) are well-established, and the practical activity (<s>vyavahāra</s>) based on them [is also well-established];
in the statement of the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>, no purpose is known. || 2 ||

children.text: iha vacanam uccārayatā vimṛśya-bhāṣiṇā pratyavamṛśyaṃ, kim idaṃ māmakaṃ vacanaṃ śrotṛ-saṃskārâdhāyakam uta nêti. itarathā paryālocita-kāritâsya hīyate. śrotṛ-saṃskārâdhāyakaṃ ced uccārayaty, anyathā viparyaya iti. etat tu pramāṇa-lakṣaṇa-vākyaṃ sakala-janânādi-prarūḍhârtha-pratyāyakatvād aśrotṛ-saṃskārâdhāyakam, yata āha:
children.translated_text: Here, one who is uttering a statement, if speaking reflectively, should consider: 'Does this statement of mine produce a dispositional impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) in the listener, or not?' Otherwise, the effectiveness of one who acts after deliberation is diminished. If it produces a dispositional impression in the listener, [it is well]; otherwise, the reverse. But this statement of the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>, since it conveys a meaning that has been familiar to all people since beginningless time, does not produce a [new] dispositional impression in the listener. Therefore [the objector] says:
meaning 'firmly rooted,' not 'to be proved now.'

children.text: pratyakṣâdīni, parokṣa-gata-bhedâpekṣayā bahu-vacanaṃ vyakti-bhede sāmānyam api kathañcid bhidyata iti-darśanârtham. tathā hi: tad avivakṣita-vyaktikam eka-rūpatāṃ bibharti pramāṇam iti; vyakty-avacchedena punar avacchidyamānaṃ nānātāmādatte pratyakṣânumāna-śābdāni pramāṇānîti, vyakti-vyatiriktâvyatirikta-rūpatvāt tasya. tathā hi: śabdāc cakṣurâder vā dūrād vṛkṣa iti pratyaye dhava-khadira-palāśâdi-viśeṣânapekṣayā sādhāraṇaṃ vṛkṣatvam eva cakāsti, tasmāt tat tebhyo bhinnaṃ, tad-vyatirekiṇâkāreṇa jñāne pratibhāsanād, ghaṭâdivat. parisphuṭa-dhava-khadira-palāśâdi-viśeṣâvalokana-velāyāṃ tu na tad, atirekiṇā rūpeṇa prakāśata ity abhinnaṃ, tad-avyatiriktasya saṃvedanāt, tat-svarūpavat. viśeṣâbhinnam eva rūpaṃ tāttvikaṃ sāmānyasya, tasyâiva dāha-pākâdy-artha-kriyā-kṣamatvād, bhinnaṃ punaḥ kalpanā-buddhi-viṭhapitatvād avastu-rūpam iti cen, na, dvayoḥ prakāśamānayor ekasya nihnotum aśakyatvāt. anyathā bhinnam eva rūpaṃ svābhāvikam itarat tu kalpanā-buddhi-darśitam ity api vadatāṃ na vadana-bhaṅgaḥ syāt. artha-kriyā-kāritâviśeṣas tu bhinne 'pi rūpe na durupapādas, tasyâpi jñāna-sādhāraṇa-vyavahāra-karaṇa-dakṣatvāt. na cârtha-kriyā vastu-lakṣaṇam iti nivedayiṣyāmas, tasmāt sarvatra bhinnâbhinnau sāmānya-viśeṣāv iti darśanârtho bahu-vacana-nirdeśaḥ. āsatāṃ tāvat pramāṇāni.
children.translated_text: i.e., <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and the like. The plural is used with reference to the division into indirect [subtypes]; [this is] to show that even the universal is somehow divided when the particulars are divided. For thus: without intending to specify particulars, [<s>pramāṇa</s>] bears a single form, as in '<s>pramāṇa</s> is [one]'; but when delimited by the delimitation of particulars, it assumes manifoldness, as in '<s>pratyakṣa</s>, <s>anumāna</s>, and <s>śābda</s> are [the] <s>pramāṇas</s>' — because its nature is both non-different and different from the particulars. For thus: in the cognition 'It is a tree' [arising] from a word or from the eye, etc. at a distance, without regard to the specific [differences of] <s>dhava</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, and the like, only the common property of tree-ness shines forth; therefore that [universal] is different from those [particulars], since it appears in cognition with a form that is distinct from them, like a pot, etc. But at the time of observing the specific [differences of] <s>dhava</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, etc. clearly, it does not manifest with a form that is additional [to them], and so it is non-different, since what is non-different from them is cognized, like their own essential nature. The real form of the universal is precisely non-different from the particulars, since only that [particular form] is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) such as burning, cooking, etc. But if [one objects that] the different [form] is a mere fabrication of conceptual thought (<s>kalpanā-buddhi</s>) and hence unreal — no, because when both are manifest, it is impossible to deny one of the two. Otherwise, there would be no inconsistency for those who say the opposite — that the different form is natural and the other is merely presented by conceptual thought. And the lack of distinction in causal efficacy is not difficult to explain even for the different form, since it too is capable of producing the common practical activity of cognition. And we shall not assert that causal efficacy is the defining characteristic of reality. Therefore, the use of the plural is to show that everywhere the universal and the particular are both different and non-different. Let the <s>pramāṇas</s> be for now.
'And the practical activity (<s>vyavahāra</s>) based on them' —

children.text: -śabdo 'pi-śabdârthaḥ. tenâyam artho: yad-arthaṃ pramāṇa-parīkṣaṇam asāv api jala-pāna-śīta-trāṇâdir vyavahāro 'nādi-prarūḍhaḥ, tan nirarthakaṃ pramāṇa-lakṣaṇâbhidhānam ity abhiprāyavān api paraḥ paruṣatā-parijihīrṣayâtmano 'nyathā prāha:
children.translated_text: has the meaning of 'also' (<s>api</s>). Thus the meaning is: the practical activity (<s>vyavahāra</s>) too — such as drinking water, protection from cold, and so on — for the sake of which the examination of <s>pramāṇas</s> [would be undertaken], is also firmly rooted since beginningless time; hence the statement of the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> is purposeless. Even though [the opponent] has this intent, out of a desire to avoid harshness, he states his own [view] differently:
'In the statement of the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>' —
[meaning:] in the stating of the unique property of <s>pramāṇa</s> that is capable of distinguishing [<s>pramāṇa</s>] from what is other than it,

children.text: tat-phalam, atisūkṣmatvāt tāvakâbhisandher iti kākvā praśnayaty ulluṇṭhayati cêti. kiṃ ca, pramāṇa-lakṣaṇam aniścitaṃ vâbhidhīyate, niścitaṃ vā svarūpeṇêti pakṣa-dvayam. na tāvad aniścitam, aniścitasya lakṣaṇatvâyogād, unmattaka-virutavat. atha niścitaṃ, tat kim apramāṇāt pramāṇād vā. na tāvad apramāṇād, apramāṇasya niścāyakatvâyogāt. yadi punar apramāṇam api niścāyakam iti saṅgīryeta, tadā pramāṇa-paryeṣaṇaṃ viśīryeta, nairarthakyâpatter, apramāṇād api niścāyâbhyupagamāt. atha pramāṇāt, tat kim alakṣaṇaṃ lakṣaṇôpetaṃ vā. alakṣaṇaṃ cen niścāyakaṃ pramāṇam, tarhi sarva-pramāṇānāṃ lakṣaṇâbhidhānam anarthakaṃ, tad-vyatirekeṇâpy artha-niścaya-siddher, bhavad-abhipreta-lakṣaṇa-niścāyaka-pramāṇavat. atha lakṣaṇôpetaṃ, tatrâpi vikalpa-yugalam anuvārita-prasaram anudhāvati: tal-lakṣaṇaṃ niścitam aniścitaṃ vā. na tāvad aniścitaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ lakṣyaṃ lakṣayati. niścayo 'pi pramāṇād apramāṇād vā. apramāṇān niścayâsiddheḥ pramāṇād iti vaktavyam. tad apy alakṣaṇaṃ salakṣaṇaṃ vā. alakṣaṇatve pūrvasyârtha-grahaṇe kiṃ kṣūṇam. salakṣaṇatve tal-lakṣaṇaṃ nirṇītam anirṇītaṃ vêti tad evâvartate. tan na pramāṇa-lakṣaṇâbhidhānôpāyo 'sti, tasmāt prasiddhāni pramāṇānîty aṅgī-kartavyam iti.
children.translated_text: i.e., a result of that [statement]; because your intention is too subtle — thus [the opponent] asks with irony and mocks. Furthermore, [one may ask:] is the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> stated as undetermined or as determined in its own nature? — this is the twofold alternative. Not, in the first place, as undetermined, because what is undetermined is unfit to be a definition, like the babbling of a madman. But if determined — then is that [determination] from a non-<s>pramāṇa</s> or from a <s>pramāṇa</s>? Not, in the first place, from a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>, since a non-<s>pramāṇa</s> is unfit to determine. If it were conceded that even a non-<s>pramāṇa</s> can determine, then the search for <s>pramāṇas</s> would collapse, since purposelessness would follow from the admission that determination is possible even from a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>. But if from a <s>pramāṇa</s> — is that [<s>pramāṇa</s>] without a definition or endowed with a definition? If a <s>pramāṇa</s> without a definition can determine, then the statement of a definition for all <s>pramāṇas</s> is pointless, since the determination of objects is accomplished even without it, just like the <s>pramāṇa</s> that determines the definition you intend. But if [it is] endowed with a definition, even there the twofold alternative follows in unimpeded succession: is that definition determined or undetermined? An undetermined definition does not characterize the characterized [object]. And the determination [of that definition] is either from a <s>pramāṇa</s> or from a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>. Since determination from a non-<s>pramāṇa</s> is not established, it must be said to be from a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Is that [<s>pramāṇa</s>] too without or with a definition? If without a definition, what was lacking in the former's apprehension of objects? If with a definition, then the same [regress] recurs: is that definition determined or not? Therefore, there is no means of stating the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>; hence [the <s>pramāṇas</s>] must be accepted as well-established.

children.text: adhunâcāryo gṛhītas tāvakīno 'bhiprāyo 'smābhir iti paraṃ pratyāyayaṃs tan-matam anudrāvya tad evânumanyamānas tathâpi lakṣaṇôkteḥ sāphalyamāvedayann āha:
children.translated_text: Now the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), indicating 'Your intention has been grasped by us,' [and] in order to convince the opponent, pursues his doctrine, accepts it as stated, and yet reveals the fruitfulness of stating the definition, says:
In the statement of the definition of the well-established <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition), the purpose
would be the removal of confusion (<s>vyāmoha</s>) regarding them, for those whose minds are deluded, in this [world]. || 3 ||
This has been stated by you, namely that
i.e., in the domain of stating the unique property —

children.text: phalaṃ, kim iti śeṣas, tad etad ayuktam. yato yady api pratiprāṇi-prasiddhāni pramāṇāny, anyathā tat-kṛta-nikhila-vyavahārôccheda-prasaṅgāt, tad-ucchede ca dṛṣṭa-hāny-ādy-āpatteḥ, tathâpi kecid vitata-mohâvaṣṭabdhântaḥ-karaṇās tat-svarūpam anubhavanto 'pi na lakṣayanti, tatas tān avalokayatām asmākaṃ tad-viṣaya-kṛpā-parīta-cetasāṃ yathâvasthita-pramāṇa-lakṣaṇâvir-bhāvana-dvāreṇa vyāmoham eteṣām apasārayāma iti pramāṇa-lakṣaṇâbhidhānaṃ prati pravartate cetaḥ. tad idaṃ prayojanaṃ:
children.translated_text: [i.e.,] the result — 'what [is it]?' is the remainder. That is incorrect. Because even though the <s>pramāṇas</s> are well-established for every living being — otherwise, the absurd consequence of the cessation of all practical activity based on them would follow, and upon that cessation, the absurd consequence of the loss of what is seen, and so forth — nevertheless, certain people whose inner faculty is seized by extensive delusion, even while experiencing their essential nature, do not apprehend it. Therefore, for us who observe them, whose minds are pervaded by compassion regarding them, [the thought arises:] 'Let us dispel their confusion through the means of manifesting the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> as it actually is' — thus the mind proceeds toward the statement of the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>. This is the purpose:
'The removal of confusion regarding them would [result]' —

children.text: viparītâbhyupagamavatāṃ viparyāsa-lakṣaṇas tīrthyānāṃ pramāṇâpramāṇa-viveka-vikalānām, anadhyavasāyâtmakas tu mugdha-buddhīnāṃ laukikānām, tasya
children.translated_text: [which is] characterized by wrong apprehension (<s>viparyāsa</s>) for the <s>tīrthyas</s> (heterodox teachers) who hold wrong views and who lack the discrimination between <s>pramāṇa</s> and non-<s>pramāṇa</s>; but [which is] characterized by non-determination (<s>anadhyavasāya</s>) for worldly people of dull intellect; of that [confusion],
meaning cessation, through the understanding of the correct definition — that is the meaning; that [removal]
i.e., would come about. For whom? He says:
gripped by wrong apprehension, having become perplexed —
[meaning] the inner faculty — those whose [mind is such] are so designated; of them;

children.text: ti loke -- tad ayaṃ tātparyârthaḥ. yady anādi prasiddhaṃ pramāṇa-lakṣaṇaṃ prati na kecid api vyāmuhyeyus tadā yad bhavadbhiḥ prāg udagrāhi: ‘nirarthakaṃ pramāṇa-lakṣaṇâbhidhānam'; iti tad yuktam eva syāt. na câitad evaṃ; tatra vyāmūḍhānāṃ darśanāt. etena yad adāyi dūṣaṇaṃ ‘pramāṇa-lakṣaṇam aniścitaṃ niścitaṃ vâbhidhīyata'; ity-ādi tad api siddha-sādhyatā-madhya-pratibaddhatvān na bādhâvidhāyy asmākam iti mantavyam. vyāmūḍha-manaso 'pi prati pramāṇa-lakṣaṇa-prakāśane tal lagatîti cen, na, sva-saṃvedana-siddhasya vacanena prakāśanāt, tasya vyāmohâpoha eva vyāpārāt. yathā vivikta-bhū-talâvalokane 'py adhyakṣāt yo ghaṭâdi-vaiviktyaṃ na pratipadyate, kudarśana-vyāmohāt, taṃ pratyucyeta: ‘nâsty atra ghaṭa, upalambha-kāraṇa-samagratāyām apy anupalambhād', vaiviktyaṃ hi tatrâdhyakṣa-siddhaṃ, vacanād vyāmoho nivartyeta; tathêhâpi vidvadbhir draṣṭavyam. nirṇītaṃ tal-lakṣaṇam adhyakṣeṇa, tasya vyavasāya-rūpatvād, vacanaṃ punar viparītâropa-nirākaraṇe vyāpriyata iti sthitam. tad evaṃ pramāṇa-lakṣaṇaṃ sāmānyena pratipādya tad-gataṃ kucodyaṃ paryahāry ācāryeṇa.
children.translated_text: means 'in the world.' This then is the purport: if no one at all were confused regarding the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> that has been well-established since beginningless time, then what was stated by you earlier — 'the statement of the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> is purposeless' — would indeed be correct. But this is not so, since those who are deluded regarding it are observed. By this, the objection that was raised — 'is the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> stated as undetermined or determined?' — and so forth, that too, being caught in the middle of proving what is already established (<s>siddha-sādhyatā</s>), should be understood as not creating a difficulty for us. If [one objects:] the illumination of the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> to those of deluded minds too would [similarly] be open [to the regress] — no, because what is established through <s>sva-saṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) is being illuminated through words, and the operation [of words] is precisely the removal of confusion regarding that. Just as when someone, even upon observing an empty ground-surface, does not understand the absence of a pot, etc. from that direct perception, due to the confusion of false seeing, one would say to him: 'There is no pot here, because it is not apprehended even when all conditions for apprehension are complete' — for the absence [of the pot] there is established by direct perception; and the confusion would be removed by the statement. So too here should the learned understand. The definition has been determined by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception), since it has the nature of ascertainment; the statement, however, operates in the removal of false superimposition. Thus it is established. In this way, the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) has demonstrated the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> in general and has dispelled the petty objections regarding it.

children.text: adhunā tad-viṣayām eva saṃkhyā-vipratipattiṃ nirācikīrṣatā ye pratyakṣa-parokṣa-lakṣaṇe pramāṇa-vyaktī prāk prakrānte, tayor api lakṣaṇaṃ prati vipratipadyante 'pare. atas tal-lakṣaṇam api vaktavyam iti tāvat pratyakṣa-lakṣaṇam abhidhātukāma āha:
children.translated_text: Now, wishing to resolve the disagreement concerning the enumeration [of <s>pramāṇas</s>] pertaining to that very [subject], [and noting that] some disagree also regarding the definitions of the two particular instances of <s>pramāṇa</s> — namely, the definitions of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>parokṣa</s> (indirect cognition) — that were previously set forth, and therefore that their definitions too must be stated, [the author], wishing first to state the definition of <s>pratyakṣa</s>, says:
That cognition which apprehends an object directly (<s>aparokṣatayā</s>) —
such is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception); the other is to be known as <s>parokṣa</s> (indirect cognition), with reference to apprehension. || 4 ||
this is the indication of the definiendum (<s>lakṣya</s>);
this is the indication of the definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). '<s>Parokṣa</s>' [means] beyond the range of the senses (<s>akṣa-gocara-atīta</s>); other than that is

children.text: , tad-bhāvas tattā tayā, sākṣāt-kṛtatayêti yāvat. aryata ity
children.translated_text: the state of that is its '-ness' (<s>tattā</s>); by that [quality], meaning 'in the mode of direct apprehension' (<s>sākṣāt-kṛtatayā</s>). '<s>Artha</s>' (object) means that which is cognized —
meaning that which is understood, that is the essence; or
[meaning] that which is desired by those who seek causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) such as burning, cooking, etc. — that is the meaning. Of that [object],

children.text: vyavasāyâtmakatayā sākṣāt paricchedakaṃ yaj jñānaṃ, tad
children.translated_text: meaning that cognition which, through the nature of ascertainment (<s>vyavasāya</s>), directly delimits [the object] — that

children.text: itîdṛg eva pratyakṣam iti saṇṭaṅkaḥ. tatra jñāna-grahaṇena yat
children.translated_text: means 'just of this kind is <s>pratyakṣa</s>' — thus is the connection. Therein, by the word 'cognition' (<s>jñāna</s>), what

children.text: prāhuḥ: ‘śrotr-ādi-vṛttiḥ pratyakṣam'; iti tat tiras-karoti, śrotr-ādīnāṃ prakṛti-vikāratayā tad-vṛtter vyāpāra-lakṣaṇāyā jaḍatayā pratyakṣatvâyogād; artha-paricchitti-hetutayā pratyakṣatve ālokâdi-jaḍa-kāraṇa-kalāpa-vyāpārasyâpi pratyakṣatâpadyeta, viśeṣâbhāvād iti.
children.translated_text: They say: 'Perception is the operation of the ear and the other [sense-organs].' This [the author] refutes, because the ear and the like, being modifications of material nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), their operation — which has the character of activity — being insentient, is unsuitable as <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception); if it were perceptual on the grounds of being a cause of the ascertainment of objects, then the operation of the aggregate of insentient causes such as light and the like would also turn out to be perceptual, since there is no distinguishing feature [between them].
being dependent on the word 'apprehension and observation' (<s>grahaṇekṣayā</s>)

children.text: ti vakṣyamāṇa-pada-sāpekṣatvād, amunā bahir api ye 'rtha-kalâkalana-vikalaṃ sakalam api jñānaṃ pralapanti tān nirasyati; svâṃśa-grahaṇe hy antaḥ-saṃvedanaṃ vyāpriyate yathā -- tathā bahir apîtarathârthavaj jñāna-santānântarāṇy api viśīryeran, svapna-dṛṣṭântena tad-anumānasyôpaplava-mātratâpatteḥ, sva-vijñānasyâiva tathā tathā vijṛmbhaṇāt. tathā ca pramāṇa-prameya-pratipādya-pratipādaka-kārya-kāraṇa-bhāvâdayaḥ pralīyerann, ātma-vyatirekeṇâtmīya-pūrvôttara-kṣaṇayor api jñānasya pravṛtti-nirodhâpatteḥ. advaya-vijñāna-tattva-sādhanenânukūlam ācarasîti cet, syād etat, yadi bhavataḥ pramāṇa-paridṛṣṭa-sakala-vyavahārôcchedena kudarśana-vāsanâhitâdṛṣṭâdvaya-tattva-parikalpanāt pratikūlaṃ na syāt. tan nârtha-viraheṇa bahiḥ-pramāṇa-bhūta-jñānôllāso 'sti, nirhetukatva-prasaṅgād iti.
children.translated_text: to be stated [later], by this [the author] refutes those who maintain that all cognition, even externally, is devoid of any contact with the aspects of objects. For [if maintained that] inner self-awareness (<s>antaḥsaṃvedana</s>) functions in the apprehension of its own aspect — then in the same way externally too, otherwise the continua of other cognitions would also disintegrate as being without real objects, since the inference thereof would turn out to be nothing but a disturbance, as illustrated by the dream example, because cognition itself manifests in various ways. Furthermore, the relations of means-of-knowledge and object-of-knowledge, that-which-is-to-be-expressed and that-which-expresses, effect and cause, and so forth would dissolve — since, apart from the self, cognition could not function or cease even with respect to its own earlier and later moments. If [you say] 'I proceed in accordance with establishing the reality of non-dual consciousness (<s>advayavijñāna</s>),' this would be so if it were not contrary [to your position] — but it is contrary, since by destroying all empirical transactions ascertained by the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), you fabricate an unseen non-dual reality deposited by the impressions of wrong views. Therefore, without objects, there is no manifestation of cognition as an external <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), because of the implication of causelessness.

children.text: iti ca nirṇāyakaṃ draṣṭavyam, nirṇayâbhāve 'rtha-grahaṇâyogāt. tena yat
children.translated_text: this should also be understood as 'that which determines,' since without determination there can be no apprehension of the object. By this, what

children.text: pratyapādi: ‘pratyakṣaṃ kalpanâpoḍham abhrāntam'; iti tad apāstaṃ bhavati, tasya yukti-riktatvāt. tathā hi: te nirvikalpakatve 'dhyakṣasyâyuktīḥ kheṭayanti -- kilêdam artha-sāmarthyenôdīyate, sannihitârtha-kriyā-samarthârtha-grāhakatvāt. na cârthe dhvanayaḥ santi, tad-dhetu-vilakṣaṇa-kāraṇântara-janyatvāt, tataś câsāv upanipatya sva-gocaraṃ saṃvedanam utthāpayan svâkāram anukārayati. tan na tad-grāhiṇi vijñāne śabda-saṃśleṣo yuktaḥ. kiṃ ca, yady utpādakârthôpayoge 'pi taṃ tāvan na gṛhṇīyāt, saṃvedanam api tu smaraṇa-sampāditaṃ tad-abhidhāyaka-dhvani-saṃyojanaṃ pratīkṣamāṇaṃ tāvad āsīta, tarhi datto jalâñjalir artha-grahaṇasya. tathā hi: tam artham apaśyaṃs tasmin gṛhīta-saṅketaṃ tad-abhidhāyaka-dhvaniṃ nânusmaraty, upāyâbhāvād, ananusmaraṃś ca puro-vartiny arthe na yojayati, smṛty-upasthāpana-vyatirekeṇa tad-yojanâśakter, ayojayaṃś ca bhavad-abhiprāyeṇa na paśyatîti dhāndhyād āndhyamāpadyeta. yadi cêndriyajam api jñānaṃ vikalpa-kaluṣitam iṣyeta, tadā tad api mano-rājyâdi-vikalpavad vikalpântarâvir-bhāve sati nivarteta; na câitad asti, sannihita-go-piṇḍa-gocarasya cakṣurja-saṃvedanasyâśvâdi-viṣaya-vikalpôdaye 'py anivartanāt, saṃhṛta-sakala-vikalpasyâpi ca parisphuṭa-sannihitârtha-viṣaya-darśana-siddheḥ. tan nâkṣajaṃ jñānaṃ śabda-samparkam anubhavatîti.
children.translated_text: have taught — '<s>Pratyakṣa</s> (perception) is free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>) and non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>)' — that is refuted, because it is devoid of reasoning. For they brandish [supposed] reasons for the non-conceptual nature of perception — [saying] that it arises by the power of the object, since it apprehends an object capable of effective action that is present [before it]. And there are no verbal expressions (<s>dhvanis</s>) in the object, since they are produced by a cause different from the cause of the object. Therefore, [perception,] encountering [the object], generates awareness of its own domain and makes [the cognition] conform to its own form. Hence, a connection with words in the cognition that apprehends that [object] is not justified. Moreover, if [one holds that perception,] even while engaging with the object that produces it, does not apprehend it, but rather waits for a conjunction with a verbal expression designating it — [a conjunction] accomplished by memory — then a water-offering has been made to [the funeral of] object-apprehension. For, not seeing that object, [the perceiver] does not recollect the verbal expression designating it for which a convention has been grasped — due to the absence of a means [to do so]; and not recollecting, does not connect [the word] with the object present before [them] — since the capacity for such connection [exists] only through the presentation of memory; and not connecting — does not see [the object], according to your view — and so one would pass from stupidity to blindness. And if sense-born cognition too were admitted to be tainted by conceptual construction, then it too would cease upon the appearance of another concept, like the concepts of daydreaming and the like. But this is not so, since the visual awareness whose domain is a present mass of cows does not cease even when a concept concerning horses and the like arises; and since even when all concepts have been withdrawn, the clear perception of a present object is established. Therefore, sense-born cognition does not undergo contact with words.

children.text: atra pratividhīyate -- yat tāvad uktam: aśabdakârtha-sāmarthyôdbhavatvād dhvani-rahitam adhyakṣam iti, tad ayuktaṃ, na hi śabdâsampṛktârthajam ity etāvatâivâbhilāpa-vinā-kṛtam iti vaktuṃ śakyam, anyathā jaḍârtha-janitam iti jaḍam api tat syāt. atha bodha-rūpa-manaskāra-sāhityān na jaḍam iti brūṣe, tathā saty abhilāpa-saṃsṛṣṭa-manaskāra-sanniyogāt sâbhilāpam api syāt. kiṃ ca, viviktāḥ paramâṇavaḥ svâkārârpaṇa-dvāreṇa sva-gocaraṃ jñānam utpādayantaḥ katham asantam ātmani svâvayava-vyāpinaṃ kālântara-saṃcariṣṇum ākāraṃ tatra prathayanti. vibhramād iti cen, na, nêdānīm arthe yad asti tad eva pratibhāti, tatrâsato 'pi sthūrâkārasya pratibhāsanāt. tathā śabdo 'pi. yady avidyamāno 'rthe tad-grāhiṇi jñāne pratibhāseta kiṃ kṣūyeta? yac côktam: ‘smaraṇa-janita-śabda-saṃyojanaṃ pratīkṣamānam arthôpayoge 'pi yady āsītêty'-ādi yāvad ‘āndhyam āpadyeta', tat tāvaka-pakṣe 'pi samānam. tathā hi: svalakṣaṇa-viṣayêndriyaja-nirvikalpaka-jñāna-sadbhāve 'pi na tāvad idaṃ-tayânidaṃ-tayā vârtha-vyavasthitir, yāvad vidhi-pratiṣedha-dvāreṇa vikalpa-yugalakaṃ pāścātyaṃ nodayate, yatrâivâṃśe vikalpaṃ janayati, tatrâivâsya pramāṇatêti-vacanān, nirvikalpakasya sato 'pi vyavahāraṃ praty asat-kalpatvāt. sa ca vikalpaḥ saṅketa-kāla-bhāvitam abhilāpa-sāmānyam anusmarata evôtpattum arhati, abhilāpa-sāmānya-smaraṇa-bījaṃ ca kutaḥ prabudhyeta? tādṛśa-darśanād iti cen, nanu tad api darśanaṃ nirvikalpakatvād arthaṃ nâtiśete, tat kathaṃ sāmānya-viṣaya-vikalpa-bījaṃ prabodhayet? arthaḥ punaḥ sāmānya-vyavasāyâtmikāṃ buddhiṃ na janayed iti bhavatāṃ kadāgrahaḥ. tad arthavat tad-viṣayaṃ darśanaṃ vyavasāya-śūnyatvān nâbhilāpa-sāmānya-gocara-smaraṇa-bījaṃ prabodhayati; tad aprabuddhaṃ na smaraṇaṃ janayaty; ajātaṃ smaraṇaṃ na śabdaṃ yojayaty; ayojitaḥ śabdo nârthaṃ niścāyayaty; aniścito 'rtho na vyavahāram avataraty; anavatīrṇo nâdṛṣṭād viśiṣyate; aviśiṣṭaḥ pramātur āndhyaṃ lakṣayatîti. tasmād yathā kathañcin-nirṇayâbhāvāt svayam apratītam api nirvikalpaka-darśanaṃ vāsanā-prabodha-dvāreṇa vikalpam utthāpyâtma-vyāpāram abhilāpayati katicid-aṃśa-viṣayaṃ, tathârtho 'pi yadi cakṣur-ādi-sāmagry-antaḥ-pātitvenâpratīta eva svayaṃ, tathā-svabhâvatvāt, saṅketa-kāla-bhāvitâbhilāpa-sāmānya-viṣayâtma-saṃskāra-prabodha-dvāreṇâtma-viṣayam abhilāpa-saṃsṛṣṭaṃ saṃvedanam ullāsayen nâtyantam ayuktaṃ paśyāmaḥ. na câyaṃ savikalpako bodho mano-rājyâdi-vikalpa-kalpaś, cakṣurâdi-sāmagrī-sampādyatvād, itarasya tu mano-mātra-prabhavatvāt. ataḥ kathaṃ tad-vikalpântarâvir-bhāve nivarteta? mānasa-vikalpasyâiva vikalpântareṇa nivartanād, asya tu kāraṇa-sāmarthyena balāt pravṛtteḥ. etena saṃhṛta-sakala-vikalpâvasthāyāṃ nâiṣa prāduḥṣyād ity etad api pratikṣiptam, asya pramātur icchayā saṃhartum aśakyatvān, mānasa-vikalpa-saṃharaṇa eva tat-sāmarthyôpapatter iti. etac ca śabda-sampṛkta-pratyakṣa-pakṣād apy ekânta-nirvikalpaka-pratyakṣa-pakṣasya pāpīyastāṃ darśayadbhir asmābhir udagrāhi.
children.translated_text: Here [the Jain author] provides a counter-argument: As for what was said — that perception is devoid of verbal expression because it arises by the power of the object which is without words — that is unjustified. For, merely from the fact that it is born from an object not conjoined with words, one cannot say it is devoid of verbal expression; otherwise, since it is born from an insentient object, it would also be insentient. If you say it is not insentient due to its conjunction with mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) whose nature is awareness — then, in that case, due to its conjunction with mental attention that is associated with verbal expression, it would also be accompanied by verbal expression. Moreover, how do discrete <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms), producing cognition of their own domain through the door of imparting their own form, project onto it a form that does not exist in themselves — a form pervading their own parts, persisting across time? If [you say] through error — no, for it is not the case that only what exists in the object appears [in cognition], since the gross form also appears though it does not exist there [in the atoms]. Likewise with words. If [a word,] not existing in the object, were to appear in the cognition that apprehends it — what would be lost? As for what was said — 'if, even while engaging with the object, [perception] were to wait for the conjunction of words generated by memory, ... [it would lead to] blindness' — that is equally [a problem] in your own position. For even granted the existence of a non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) sense-born cognition whose object is the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), there is no determination of the object as 'this' or 'not-this' until a subsequent pair of concepts arises through the door of affirmation and negation — since [you yourself say] 'its status as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) applies only to that very aspect in which it generates a concept'; thus, even though the non-conceptual [perception] exists, it is as good as non-existent with respect to empirical activity. And that concept can arise only through recollecting a verbal universal (<s>abhilāpa-sāmānya</s>) conditioned at the time of convention. And from what would the seed of the recollection of the verbal universal be awakened? If [you say] from seeing [something] of that kind — but surely that seeing too, being non-conceptual, does not go beyond the object; so how would it awaken the seed of a concept concerning a universal? That the object should not generate a cognition whose nature is a determination of a universal — this is your obstinate prejudice. Therefore, that perception of the object, being empty of determination, does not awaken the seed of recollection directed at the domain of the verbal universal; that [seed], un-awakened, does not generate recollection; recollection, not having arisen, does not connect the word; the word, unconnected, does not bring about the ascertainment of the object; the object, unascertained, does not enter into empirical activity; [the object] that has not entered [activity] is not distinguished from the unseen; and [the object] not distinguished marks the blindness of the cognizer. Therefore, since there is no determination in any way, even the non-conceptual perception — itself unrecognized — through the door of awakening latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), raises a concept and causes its own operation to be expressed, [though] directed at only some aspects [of the object]; likewise, even if the object itself is unrecognized on its own — being included within the aggregate of causes such as the eye and the like — since it is of such a nature, we do not see it as entirely unreasonable that it should, through the door of awakening the latent impressions of the verbal universal conditioned at the time of convention concerning itself, give rise to an awareness of itself that is conjoined with verbal expression. And this conceptual awareness is not like the concepts of daydreaming and the like, because it is produced by the aggregate of causes such as the eye and the like, whereas the other [concepts] arise from the mind alone. Therefore, how would it cease upon the appearance of another concept? For only a mental concept is displaced by another concept, whereas this one proceeds with force due to the power of its causes. By this, the [objection] that 'in the state where all concepts have been withdrawn, this [perception] would not manifest' is also refuted, since this cannot be withdrawn at the cognizer's will — the capacity for such [withdrawal] applying only to the withdrawal of mental concepts. And this [argument] was put forward by us in an emphatic manner, showing that the position of exclusively non-conceptual perception is even worse than the position of perception conjoined with words.

children.text: paramârthataḥ punaḥ pratyakṣe sākṣāc chabdôllekho nêṣyate, viśada-vyavasāyenârtha-sākṣāt-karaṇa-caturatvāt tasya. kevalaṃ tad api sannihitaṃ parisphuṭaṃ svâvayava-vyāpinaṃ kālântara-saṃcariṣṇuṃ sthagita-kṣaṇa-vivartam alakṣita-paramâṇu-pārimāṇḍalyaṃ padârthântaraiḥ saha samānâsamānâkāraṃ sva-paramâṇūnāṃ sāmānyâkāraṃ stambhâdhikaṃ padârthaṃ gocarayatîti savikalpakam ity ucyate, para-parikalpita-kṣaṇa-kṣayi-vivikta-paramâṇu-lakṣaṇa-svalakṣaṇa-grahaṇa-pravaṇa-nirvikalpaka-pratyakṣa-pratiṣedhârthaṃ kathañcid-abhilāpa-saṃsarga-yogya-gocaratā-darśanârthaṃ vā. evaṃ ca pratyakṣa-gocarī-kṛte 'rthe saṃjñā-saṃjñi-sambandha-grahaṇâdayas tad-viṣayāḥ śābda-vyavahārāḥ sarva eva nirupacaritā ghaṭanta ity uktaṃ bhavati. yadi punaḥ śabda-saṃsarga-yogya-pratibhāsam adhyakṣaṃ na syāt, tataḥ ko doṣa iti ced, vikalpânutthānena sakala-vyavahārôccheda-prasaṅgaḥ. tathā hi: nirvyavasāyaṃ darśanam atyanta-pāṭavôpetam api smṛti-bījâdhānaṃ tad-uttara-kāla-bhāvi vā tādṛśârtha-darśanaṃ tat-prabodhanam abhyāsa-vāsanā-pāṭave 'pi na vidhātum alaṃ, yataḥ sāmānya-vikalpôtpattyā vyavahāraḥ pravarteta, kṣaṇikatvâdiṣu sakala-kālaṃ nirvikalpakâdhyakṣa-dṛṣṭatayâbhyupagateṣv api tad-adarśanāt. tasmād yatra kutracid arthâṃśe pāścātya-vyavahāra-pravṛttis tatra prācīnaṃ saṃvedanaṃ nirṇāyakam abhyupagantavyam, anyathā kṣaṇikatvâdy-aṃśavat sarvâṃśeṣu vyavahāraḥ pralīyeta. tan na kadācana kalpanâpoḍhatvaṃ pratyakṣasya pramātur api pratīti-gocara-cāritām anubhavati. apratītaṃ câstîti śraddhātuṃ duḥśakam, atiprasaṅgād ity alakṣaṇam.
children.translated_text: In the ultimate sense, however, the direct inscription of words in perception is not accepted [by us], since it [perception] is skilled at directly realizing the object through clear determination. Nevertheless, even that [perception] is called <s>savikalpaka</s> (conceptual), because it apprehends an object that is present, clearly manifest, pervading its own parts, persisting across time, with its momentary fluctuations concealed, with the sphericality of its atoms unperceived, [sometimes] having the same and [sometimes] different forms in relation to other entities, [and having] the universal form of its own atoms — an entity such as a pillar and so forth. [It is so called] for the purpose of refuting the <s>nirvikalpaka pratyakṣa</s> (non-conceptual perception) as conceived by the opponents — characterized by the apprehension of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) defined as momentary, perishable, discrete atoms — or for showing that its object is somehow fit for conjunction with verbal expression. And thus it is stated that when the object has been brought within the range of perception, all verbal transactions concerning it — such as the apprehension of the relation of name, named object, and their connection — are non-metaphorical and coherent. But if perception were not to have an appearance fit for conjunction with words, then what fault [would follow]? The implication would be the destruction of all empirical activity, due to the non-arising of concepts. For perception without determination, even if endowed with utmost acuity, is unable to deposit a seed of memory or — even if [there is] a later perception of an object of such a kind — to awaken that [seed], even with the maturity of latent impressions from practice; since empirical activity would proceed [only] through the arising of a concept of a universal, and since [such universal-concept] is not seen [to arise] even though [objects] such as momentariness and the like are accepted as having been always perceived by non-conceptual direct perception. Therefore, wherever there is subsequent empirical activity concerning any aspect of an object, there the prior awareness must be accepted as determinative; otherwise, empirical activity would dissolve in all aspects, just as in the aspect of momentariness and the like. Thus, the quality of being free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍhatva</s>) never attains, even for the cognizer, the status of being within the range of experience. And that something unrecognized exists — this is hard to believe, due to over-extension; hence it is a faulty definition.

children.text: abhrāntatvam api na jāghaṭīti, bhavad-abhiprāyeṇa sthira-sthūrârtha-grāhiṇaḥ saṃvedanasya viparyasta-rūpatvāt, tad-viparītasya tu svapna-kāle 'py aprakāśamānatvāt. tad yadi yathâvasthitârtha-grāhitvam abhrāntatvaṃ, tan na sambhavaty eva, vivikta-kṣaṇa-kṣayi-paramâṇūnāṃ kadācid apy apratibhāsāt, teṣāṃ ca pāramārthikatvāt. atha vyāvahārikâbhiprāyeṇa yad idaṃ ghaṭâdikaṃ svalakṣaṇam artha-kriyā-kṣamaṃ, tatra yan na bhrāmyati tad abhrāntam ity abhipretaṃ, tarhi kalpanâpoḍha-padam utsāraṇīyam, idānīm anena sahâvasthānâbhāvād, vyavahārâvatāriṇo ghaṭâdi-svalakṣaṇasya nirṇayenâiva grahaṇād, anyathā vyavahārâpravṛtter, dṛṣṭasyâpy adṛṣṭânatiśayanāt. tasmād vyavasāyâtmakam adhyakṣam ity etad eva cārv iti sthitam.
children.translated_text: Non-erroneousness (<s>abhrāntatva</s>) also does not hold good, since — according to your view — the awareness that apprehends a stable, gross object has an erroneous form, while its opposite [a cognition apprehending momentary atoms] does not manifest even in the dream state. Therefore, if non-erroneousness means apprehending the object as it really is, that is simply impossible, since discrete, momentary, perishable <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms) never appear [in perception], and they alone are ultimately real. If, on the other hand, it is intended in the conventional sense — that with respect to this <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) such as a pot and so forth, which is capable of effective action, that [cognition] which does not err is non-erroneous — then the term <s>kalpanāpoḍha</s> (free from conceptual construction) must be dropped, since it cannot now coexist with [non-erroneousness]; for the apprehension of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> of pot and so forth that enters into empirical activity is precisely through determination; otherwise, empirical activity would not proceed, and what is seen would not be superior to what is unseen. Therefore, [the position] that perception is of the nature of determination — this alone is elegant. Thus it is established.
By the word '<s>aparokṣatayā</s>' (by way of being non-remote),

children.text: ty anena tu parokṣa-lakṣaṇa-saṅkīrṇatām adhyakṣasya pariharati, tasya sākṣāt-kāritayā artha-grahaṇa-rūpatvād iti.
children.translated_text: he [the author] removes the [possibility of] confusion of perception with the definition of <s>parokṣa</s> (indirect knowledge), since the nature of [perceptual] apprehension of the object is through direct presentation.

children.text: ity amunā tu pūrvôkta-nyāyāt sāvadhāraṇena viśeṣaṇa-kadambaka-saciva-jñānôpapradarśanāt para-parikalpita-lakṣaṇa-yuktasya pratyakṣatāṃ pratikṣipati. evaṃ ca yad āhur: "indriyârtha-sannikarṣôtpannaṃ jñānam avyapadeśyam avyabhicāri vyavasāyâtmakaṃ pratyakṣam" tathā "sat-samprayoge puruṣasyêndriyāṇāṃ buddhi-janma tat pratyakṣam" ity-ādi tad ayuktam ity uktaṃ bhavaty, apūrva-prādur-bhāvasya pramāṇa-bādhitatvād, atyantâsatāṃ śaśa-viṣāṇâdīnām apy utpatti-prasaṅgāt. tasmād idam ātma-rūpatayā vidyamānam eva viśeṣa-kṛd-dhetu-kalāpa-sannidhānāt sākṣād artha-grahaṇa-pariṇāma-rūpatayā vivarteta; tathā côtpanna-janmâdi-viśeṣaṇaṃ na sambhavet. athâivaṃ-vidhârtha-sūcakam evâitad ity ācakṣīthās, tathā saty avigānam evêty āstāṃ tāvat.
children.translated_text: By this [argument], however, from the aforementioned reasoning, through the emphatic demonstration of knowledge accompanied by a cluster of qualifying attributes, he rejects the <s>pratyakṣatva</s> (perceptual status) of [perception] endowed with characteristics fabricated by others. And thus, what they say — 'Knowledge arising from the contact of sense-organ and object, which is unnameable, unerring, and of the nature of determinate cognition, is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception)' — and likewise 'The birth of cognition in a person when the sense-organs are in contact with an existent [object], that is <s>pratyakṣa</s>' — and so forth, is shown to be unjustified, because the appearance of something entirely new is contradicted by the means of valid knowledge, and because there would be the unwanted consequence of the origination even of absolutely non-existent things such as a hare's horn. Therefore, this [cognition], existing as it does in its own essential nature, would transform — due to the proximity of a cluster of causes producing particular [modifications] — into the form of a transformation that is the direct apprehension of the object; and thus, qualifications such as 'arisen,' 'born,' etc. would not be possible. If you were to say that this is merely indicative of such an object, then in that case it would simply be <s>avigāna</s> (recognition) — but let that be for now.
Now he shows the definition of <s>parokṣa</s> (indirect cognition):

children.text: ity-ādi. aparokṣatayârthasya grāhakaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣam ity uktam, tasmād itarad asākṣād artha-grāhakaṃ jñānaṃ parokṣam iti
children.translated_text: and so forth. Knowledge that apprehends an object directly (<s>aparokṣa</s>) has been stated to be <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception); therefore, 'the other' — knowledge that apprehends an object indirectly — is <s>parokṣa</s> (indirect cognition); thus it is

children.text: avagantavyam. etad api sva-saṃvedanâpekṣayā pratyakṣam eva, bahir-arthâpekṣayā tu parokṣa-vyapadeśam aśnuta iti darśayann āha:
children.translated_text: — to be understood. This too, with reference to <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness), is indeed <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct); but with reference to external objects, it receives the designation <s>parokṣa</s> (indirect). Showing this, he says:

children.text: ti; iha grahaṇaṃ prakramād bahiḥ pravartanam ucyate, 'nyathā viśeṣaṇa-vaiyarthyāt; tasyêkṣâpekṣā tayā; bahiḥ-pravṛtti-paryālocanayêti yāvat. tad ayam artho: yady api svayaṃ pratyakṣaṃ, tathâpi liṅga-śabdâdi-dvāreṇa bahir-viṣaya-grahaṇe 'sākṣāt-kāritayā vyāpriyata iti parokṣam ity ucyate. etac ca bubhutsitârthânyathânupapannârthântara-pratīti-vaśād udaya-dharmakaṃ iti. sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-sadbhāvād ekâkāram api vipratipatti-nirākaraṇârthaṃ dvidhā bhidyate, tad yathā: anumānaṃ śābdaṃ cêti. yato 'dyâpi śabdasyârthânyathânupapannatvam eva pare na pratipadyante, na câpṛthak-kṛtasya tad-viviktaṃ vaktuṃ śakyam, ato bhedenôpanyāsaḥ.
children.translated_text: here, 'apprehension,' by the context, refers to external operation; otherwise there would be redundancy of the qualifier. Its 'reference' (<s>īkṣā</s>) [means] 'by consideration of' — that is, by consideration of [its] external operation. The meaning is this: although in itself it is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct), nevertheless, because it operates indirectly in apprehending external objects through the mediation of <s>liṅga</s> (inferential marks), <s>śabda</s> (words), and so forth, it is called <s>parokṣa</s> (indirect). And this [indirect cognition], due to the cognition of another meaning that would be otherwise inexplicable for what one desires to know, has the character of arising [from something else]. Although it is of a single form due to the existence of its general characteristic, it is divided into two for the purpose of removing disagreement, namely: <s>anumāna</s> (inference) and <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony). Since even now others do not accept that verbal testimony [operates] precisely through the otherwise-inexplicability of the meaning, and since one cannot speak of it distinctly without first separating it, therefore it is presented as a distinct [category].
There, wishing first to state the definition of <s>anumāna</s> (inference), he says:
From a <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) that is inseparable from the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved), that which ascertains the <s>sādhya</s> is regarded as
<s>anumāna</s> (inference); that is unerring, because it is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), like <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). NA_5

children.text: ihâpy anumānam iti lakṣya-nirdeśaḥ, tasya prasiddhatayā anūdyatvāt.
children.translated_text: Here too, '<s>anumāna</s>' is the indication of the definiendum, since it is mentioned as already well-known.
'That which ascertains the <s>sādhya</s> from a <s>liṅga</s> inseparable from the <s>sādhya</s>'

children.text: iti lakṣaṇa-nirdeśaḥ, tasyâprasiddhatayā vidheyatvād iti. atrâpy anumāna-śabdasya kartr-ādi-kāraka-vyutpatti-krameṇârtha-kathanaṃ pramāṇa-śabdavad draṣṭavyam. tataś cêhâpi liṅga-grahaṇa-sādhyâvinâbhāvitva-lakṣaṇa-liṅga-sambandha-smaraṇa-kālāt [Anu] paścān mīyate paricchidyate 'rtho 'numeyaḥ pāvakâdir yena jñānena tad anumānam iti. tat kiṃ-bhūtam ity āha:
children.translated_text: — this is the statement of the definition, since it is the predicate, being not yet established. Here too, the explanation of the meaning of the word '<s>anumāna</s>' through the derivational sequence of agent and other <s>kārakas</s> (syntactic relations) should be seen as analogous to that of the word '<s>pramāṇa</s>.' Accordingly, here too: subsequent to the time of apprehending the <s>liṅga</s> and remembering the connection of the <s>liṅga</s> characterized by inseparability from the <s>sādhya</s>, the object to be inferred — such as fire and the like — is measured, i.e. ascertained, by which cognition, that is <s>anumāna</s>. What kind [of cognition] is it? He says:

children.text: iti -- sādhanam arhati, sādhayituṃ vā śakya iti sādhyo 'numeya ity arthaḥ; tasya niścāyakaṃ tat-svarūpa-nirṇāyakam iti yāvat. tat kuta ity āha:
children.translated_text: — <s>sādhya</s> means that which deserves to be established, or that which is capable of being established, i.e. the object to be inferred (<s>anumeya</s>); that which ascertains it, i.e. that which determines its essential nature. From what [does it arise]? He says:

children.text: -- liṅgyate gamyate 'rtho 'nenêti liṅgaṃ hetus tasmāt. kiṃ-bhūtād ity āha:
children.translated_text: — a <s>liṅga</s> is that by which the object is indicated or known, i.e. the <s>hetu</s> (reason); from that. Of what kind? He says:

children.text: iti -- vinā bhavatîti vinâbhu, tato 'nyad avinâbhu, sādhyenâvinâbhu sādhyâvinâbhu, sādhyaṃ vimucya yan na bhavatîty arthaḥ, tasmāt sādhya-niścāyakaṃ jñānaṃ tad anumānam.
children.translated_text: — that which exists without [the <s>sādhya</s>] is <s>vinābhu</s> (separable); what is other than that is <s>avinābhu</s> (inseparable); inseparable from the <s>sādhya</s> means <s>sādhyāvinābhu</s> — the meaning is: that which does not exist apart from the <s>sādhya</s>. From such [a mark], the cognition that ascertains the <s>sādhya</s> is <s>anumāna</s>.
— is accepted by those versed in logic; this is the syntactic connection. Among these,
— by this, he wards off the confusion of <s>anumāna</s> (inference) with the definitions of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony).
— by this, he indicates the rejection of the definition of <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) devised by others.

children.text: tataś ca yat pare procuḥ -- pakṣa-dharmatvânvaya-vyatireka-lakṣaṇa-rūpa-trayôpalakṣitāni trīṇy eva liṅgāni: anupalabdhiḥ svabhāvaḥ kāryaṃ cêti; tad uktam:
children.translated_text: And thus, what others have declared — that the <s>liṅgas</s> (inferential marks), characterized by the three conditions of being a property of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus), positive concomitance, and negative concomitance, are precisely three: <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature), and <s>kārya</s> (effect) — as stated:
'In the subject to be inferred and in what is similar to it, presence; non-existence in what is absent —
the three <s>hetus</s> (reasons) are called non-apprehension, essential nature, and effect';

children.text: tathânye: "'syêdaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ saṃyogi samavāyi virodhi cêti laiṅgikam" iti, tathā: "pūrvavac cheṣavat sāmānyato-dṛṣṭam" ity-ādi -- tad bāla-pralapita-prāyam ity avagantavyaṃ, sarvatra sādhyâvinâbhāvitvasyâiva gamakatvāt, tad-rahitasya tu trailakṣaṇya-lakṣitasyâpy agamakatvād, itarathā tat-putratvâdīnām api gamakatva-prasaṅgān, niyamavat. trailakṣaṇyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ, na yat-kiñcit, tenâyam aprasaṅga iti cen, na, niyamena sādhyâvinâbhāvitvasyâivôddīpanāt; tac ced asti kiṃ trailakṣaṇyâpekṣayā, tasyâiva gamakatvāt. tathā hi: jala-candrān nabhaś-candraṃ, kṛttikôdayāc chakaṭôdayaṃ, puṣpitâika-cūtāt puṣpitâśeṣa-cūtān, candrôdayāt kumudâkara-prabodhaṃ, vṛkṣāc chāyām ity-ādi pakṣa-dharmatva-virahe 'py anumimīmahe. kālâdikas tatra dharmī samasty eva, tatra pakṣa-dharmatā liṅgasya gṛhyata iti cen, nâtiprasaṅgād, evaṃ hi śabdasyânityatve sādhye kāka-kārṣṇyâder api gamakatva-prasaktes, tatrâpi lokâder dharmiṇaḥ kalpayituṃ śakyatvāt. tathânvaya-vikalo 'py anityaḥ śabdaḥ, śrāvaṇatvād ity ayaṃ samyag-ghetutayā samarthayituṃ śakya iti, nânvayo 'pi hetor lakṣaṇam. tathā hi: tāvakâkūtenâiva sakalaṃ sattvam anityatayā kroḍī-kṛtam iti bhāva-dharmaḥ śrāvaṇatvaṃ katham anityatāṃ vihāya vipakṣe vartitum utsaheta, tad-vikalasya niḥsvabhāvatâpatter, anityatā-vinirmuktasya sattvasyâsambhavāvat. etena sâtmakaṃ jīvac-charīraṃ, prāṇâdimattvān, nirātmakatve tad-vaikalya-prasaṅgād, ghaṭâdivad ity ayam api gamako vyākhyātaḥ, sādhyârthânyathânupapannatvasyâtrâpi sadbhāvāt, pakṣa-dharmatvânvayayos tv alakṣaṇatayā pratipādanāt.
children.translated_text: and likewise others [say]: 'effect, cause, conjoined, inherent, and contradictory — these are the inferential [marks]'; and also: '<s>pūrvavat</s> (from prior), <s>śeṣavat</s> (from remainder), <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (from general observation)' and so forth — all this should be understood as mere prattle of children, because in all cases it is inseparability from the <s>sādhya</s> alone that serves as the indicator, while [a mark] devoid of that, even if characterized by the three conditions, fails to indicate. Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence that even being-the-son-of-that and the like would be indicators — just as with a fixed rule. [Objection:] The three conditions constitute the defining characteristic, not just anything, and therefore this unwanted consequence does not arise. [Reply:] No, because inseparability from the <s>sādhya</s> alone is invariably highlighted by the fixed rule. If that [inseparability] is present, what need for the three conditions, since that alone serves as the indicator? For indeed: from the reflection of the moon in water we infer the moon in the sky; from the rising of the <s>Kṛttikā</s> (Pleiades) we infer the rising of <s>Śakaṭa</s> (Hyades); from one mango tree in flower we infer all mango trees in flower; from the moonrise we infer the opening of the water-lily pond; from a tree we infer its shadow — and so on, even in the absence of being-a-property-of-the-<s>pakṣa</s>. [Objection:] In those cases, time and the like collectively constitute the <s>dharmin</s> (locus), and therein the <s>pakṣa-dharmatā</s> (being-a-property-of-the-<s>pakṣa</s>) of the <s>liṅga</s> is apprehended. [Reply:] No, because of over-extension: for in that case, when proving the impermanence of sound, even the blackness of crows and the like would become indicators, since there too one could posit the world and such as the <s>dharmin</s>. Likewise, 'sound is impermanent because it is audible' — even though devoid of positive concomitance — can be upheld as a valid reason, therefore positive concomitance too is not a defining characteristic of the <s>hetu</s>. For, by your own intention, the entirety of existence is encompassed by impermanence, so how could the property of being audible, which is a property of existents, dare to occur in the counter-domain apart from impermanence, since what lacks it would have the consequence of being essenceless, just as the existence of something free from impermanence is impossible. By this, the [reason] 'A living body possesses a self, because it possesses breath and the like — for if it were selfless, there would be the consequence of their absence — like a pot, etc.' is also explained as a valid indicator, because the otherwise-inexplicability of the meaning to be proved exists here too, while being-a-property-of-the-<s>pakṣa</s> and positive concomitance are shown to not be [necessary] defining characteristics.

children.text: tathā kārya-svabhāvânupalabdhi-rūpa-liṅga-traya-niyamo 'pi kila tādātmya-tad-utpatti-lakṣaṇa-sambandhâstitvam eteṣv evêti yaḥ kriyate, so 'py ayuktaḥ, prakṛta-sambandha-dvaya-vikalasyâpi rūpâde rasâdi-gamakatva-darśanāt. mā bhūt tasya tādātmya-tad-utpattibhyāṃ gamakatvaṃ, samavāyād bhaviṣyati, tathâpi nânyathânupapannatvam eva hetor lakṣaṇam iti yadi vaiśeṣiko manyeta, so 'nyathā nirloṭhanīyaḥ. sa hi vikalpataḥ paryanuyojyaḥ: samavāyibhyaḥ samavāyo 'bhinno bhinno vā. yady abhinnaḥ, samavāyina eva tarhi, na samavāyaḥ, tad-avyatiriktatvāt, tat-svarūpavat. bhinnaś cet, sa kathaṃ teṣu varteta: sāmastyenâhosvid eka-deśena? tad yadi sāmastyena, tad ayuktaṃ, samavāya-bahutva-prasaṅgāt, pratisamavāyi tasya parisamāptatâvāpteḥ. athâika-deśena, tad apy acāru, sâṃśatā-prasaṅgena niravayavatva-kṣateḥ, svâṃśa-vartane 'pi sāmastyâika-deśa-codyâvatārāc ca. tatrâpi sāmastya-pakṣe bahutvaṃ tad-avastham eva. eka-deśa-pakṣe tv aṃśântara-prasaṅgenânavasthā. tan na samavāya-balāt gamakatāṃ praty āśāvidheyā, tasyâiva tatra duḥsthitatvāt. etena saṃyogino 'pi gamakatā pratyuktā, samāna-dūṣaṇatvāt. virodhino 'pi viruddhâbhāva-gamakatvam anyathânupapannatvam eva sūcayati, tad-abhāve gamakatvâyogāt.
children.translated_text: Likewise, the restriction to the three types of <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark), namely <s>kārya</s> (effect), <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature), and <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), which is supposedly made on the ground that the two types of relation — <s>tādātmya</s> (identity) and <s>tadutpatti</s> (causal origination) — exist only in these, is also unjustified, because we observe that <s>rūpa</s> (form/color) and the like serve as indicators of <s>rasa</s> (taste) and the like even without the aforementioned two relations. [Objection:] Let its indicative capacity not come from <s>tādātmya</s> or <s>tadutpatti</s>; it will come from <s>samavāya</s> (inherence). [Reply:] Even so, the definition of the <s>hetu</s> is nothing but otherwise-inexplicability. If a <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> were to think thus, he should be refuted differently. For he should be cross-examined by way of alternatives: Is <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) identical with or different from the things that inhere? If identical, then it is simply the inherents themselves, not <s>samavāya</s>, since it does not differ from them, just like their own essential nature. If different, how would it subsist in them — in totality or partially? If in totality, that is unjustified, because there would be the consequence of a multiplicity of <s>samavāyas</s>, since it would be completely realized in each inherent. If partially, that too is unacceptable, because of the consequence of having parts, which would damage [its supposed] partlessness, and because even in the subsistence in its own parts, the objections of totality and partiality would recur. In the totality option there, the multiplicity [problem] remains unchanged. In the partiality option, there is an infinite regress due to [the need for] further parts. Therefore, one should not place hope in the indicative capacity [coming] from <s>samavāya</s>, since it itself is ill-established therein. By this, the indicative capacity of <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) is also refuted, since the fault is the same. The indicative capacity of what is contradictory, too, [namely] indicating the absence of what is contradicted, itself points to otherwise-inexplicability, since without that [inexplicability] there would be no indicative capacity.

children.text: evaṃ para-parikalpitam anyad api liṅga-lakṣaṇaṃ yad gamakatâṅgaṃ tad anyathânupapannatvaṃ na vyabhicarati, sādhyaṃ vinâpy upapadyamānasya gamakatā-vaikalyād iti; atrâiva vyāpake liṅga-lakṣaṇe 'ntar-bhāvanīyaṃ, viparītaṃ tu nirasanīyam iti sthitam.
children.translated_text: Thus, whatever other definition of the <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) fabricated by others [there may be], whatever element of indicative capacity it has does not deviate from otherwise-inexplicability, because something that can be accounted for even without the <s>sādhya</s> lacks indicative capacity. This [otherwise-inexplicability] is to be subsumed under the all-encompassing definition of the <s>liṅga</s>, while whatever is opposed [to it] is to be rejected. This is established.

children.text: tad evam anumāna-lakṣaṇaṃ pratipādyâdhunā yac chauddhodani-śiṣyakair nyagādi, yad uta -- bhrāntam anumānam, sāmānya-pratibhāsitvāt, tasya ca bahiḥ-svalakṣaṇe vyatirekâvyatireka-vikalpābhyām apākriyamāṇatayâyogāt, tad-rūpatayā ca tena tasyâdhyavasāyād, atasmiṃs tad-grahaṇasya ca bhrānti-lakṣaṇatvāt. prāmāṇyaṃ punaḥ praṇālikayā bahiḥ svalakṣaṇa-balâyātatvād anumānasya. tathā hi: nârthaṃ vinā tādātmya-tad-utpatti-rūpa-sambandha-pratibaddha-liṅga-sadbhāvo, na tad vinā tad-viṣayaṃ jñānaṃ, na taj-jñānam antareṇa prāg-avadhārita-sambandha-smaraṇaṃ, tad-asmaraṇe nânumānam ity, arthâvyabhicāritvād bhrāntam api pramāṇam iti saṅgīryate; tad uktam: "atasmiṃs tad-graho bhrāntir api sambandhataḥ pramêti" -- tad apākartum āha:
children.translated_text: Having thus set forth the definition of <s>anumāna</s> (inference), now [he addresses] what was said by the followers of the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s> (i.e. the Buddhists), namely: 'Inference is erroneous, because it has a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) as its appearing object, and that [universal] cannot [exist] in external <s>svalakṣaṇas</s> (unique particulars) since it is rejected by both the alternatives of being different and not different [from them], and because [inference] superimposes that [universal] as the nature of the [particular], and because apprehending something where it is not is the definition of error. Its validity, however, is [only] conventional, because the power of inference extends outward to external <s>svalakṣaṇas</s>. For: without the object, there would be no existence of the <s>liṅga</s> connected by the relation of identity or causal origination; without that, there would be no cognition having that as its object; without that cognition, there would be no recollection of the previously ascertained connection; without that recollection, there would be no inference — therefore, because it does not deviate from the object, it is accepted that even though erroneous, it is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge).' As it is said: 'Apprehending something where it is not is error; yet through connection, it is also a <s>pramāṇa</s>.' To refute this, he says:

children.text: anumānaṃ, bhrāmyati sva-gocare viparyasyatîti bhrāntaṃ, tato 'nyad
children.translated_text: — [refers to] <s>anumāna</s> (inference); 'erring' (<s>bhrānta</s>) means that which goes astray or is inverted regarding its own domain; what is other than that is

children.text: , aviparītârtha-grāhîti yāvat. iyaṃ ca pratijñā. pramīyate yathâvasthito 'rthaḥ paricchidyate 'nenêti pramāṇaṃ, tad-bhāvas tat-tvaṃ tasmāt. ayaṃ tu hetuḥ. saṅgatam akṣāṇām iti samakṣaṃ, tad iva
children.translated_text: — that is, one that apprehends the object without inversion. And this is the thesis. <s>Pramāṇa</s> means that by which an object as it actually is, is measured or ascertained; its nature (<s>tattva</s>) [means] that quality. This, however, is the reason. <s>Samakṣa</s> means 'in the presence of the senses' (<s>akṣāṇām</s>); like that,

children.text: iti dṛṣṭântaḥ. tad idam anumānasya bhrāntatā-nirākārakaṃ sampūrṇâvayavam, upanaya-nigamanayor avayava-traya-pratipādanenâivâkṣiptatvāt. pramāṇaṃ sūcitam, prayogas tv evaṃ draṣṭavyo: 'bhrāntam anumānaṃ, pramāṇatvād, iha yad yat pramāṇaṃ tat tad abhrāntaṃ yathā samakṣaṃ, tathā ca pramāṇaṃ bhavadbhir abhyupagamyate 'numānaṃ, tasmāt pramāṇatvād abhrāntam iti pratipadyantām iti. tatrârtha-vādī tāvat samakṣa-lakṣaṇe dṛṣṭânte sādhya-vikalatām āvir-bhāvayituṃ na pārayati, svayam eva samakṣasyâbhrāntatayā 'bhyupagamāt. śūnya-vādinaḥ punaḥ samastâpalāpitvāt pramāṇa-prameya-vyavahāraṃ praty ayogyatâivêti na tam adhikṛtya sva-sādhana-doṣāḥ parihartavyāḥ, sva-vacana-bādhita-pratijñatvena tad-vādôtthānâbhāvāt. tathā hi: sarvâbhāva-pratipādakaṃ vaco 'sti, nâsti vā? yady asti tarhi pratijñā-hāniḥ. atha nâsti, sakala-bhāva-siddhiḥ, pratiṣedhakâbhāvāt.
children.translated_text: Thus the example. This, then, is the complete-membered [syllogism] that refutes the charge of erroneousness against inference, since the application (<s>upanaya</s>) and conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) are already implied by the statement of the [first] three members. The <s>pramāṇa</s> [nature] has been indicated; the formal argument (<s>prayoga</s>) should be viewed thus: 'Inference is not erroneous, because it is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Whatever is a <s>pramāṇa</s> is non-erroneous, like perception (<s>samakṣa</s>). And inference is accepted by you as a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Therefore, since it is a <s>pramāṇa</s>, accept that it is non-erroneous.' Here the realist (<s>artha-vādin</s>) is first unable to show the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proved) in the example of perception, since he himself accepts perception as non-erroneous.
