children.translated_text: because of doubt about the exclusion of possession of passion and so forth, it is one of doubtful exclusion of the prover. The one of doubtful exclusion of both provable and prover is as follows: '<s>Kapila</s> and others are not free from passion, because of not having given away pieces of their own flesh even to objects of compassion, due to their minds not being pervaded by compassion.' Here the negative-agreement example [is]: 'Those who are free from passion, their minds being pervaded by compassion toward objects of compassion, have given away pieces of their own flesh, like the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.' Here, the exclusion from the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of both the provable and prover properties is doubtful; owing to the deficiency of the <s>pramāṇa</s> that would establish them, it is not known whether they possess passion or are free from passion; likewise, whether they gave away pieces of their own flesh to those deserving compassion or not. Therefore, it is one of doubtful exclusion of both provable and prover.

children.text: parair apare 'pi dṛṣṭântâbhāsās trayo 'vimṛśya-bhāṣitayā darśitāḥ. tad yathā -- avyatireko, 'pradarśita-vyatireko, viparīta-vyatirekaś cêti. te 'smābhir ayuktatvān na darśayitavyāḥ. tathā hy: avyatirekas tair darśito, yathâvīta-rāgaḥ kaścid vivakṣitaḥ puruṣo, vaktṛtvād iti. atra vaidharmya-ḍṛṣṭânto: yaḥ punar vīta-rāgo, na sa vaktā, yathôpala-khaṇḍa iti. yady api kilôpala-khaṇḍād ubhayaṃ vyāvṛttaṃ, tathâpi vyāptyā vyatirekâsiddher avyatirekitvam iti. ayuktaś câyaṃ vaktum, avyatirekitāyā hetu-doṣatvāt. yadi hi dṛṣṭânta-balenâiva vyatirekaḥ pratipādyeta, tadā tathā-vidha-sāmarthya-vikalasya tad-ābhāsatā yujyeta, na câitad asti, prāk-pravṛtta-sambandha-grahaṇa-pravaṇa-pramāṇa-gocara-smaraṇa-sampādanârthaṃ dṛṣṭântôpādānāt. na hy ekatra yo yad-abhāve na dṛṣṭaḥ, sa tad-abhāve na bhavatîti pratibandha-grāhi-pramāṇa-vyatirekeṇa sidhyaty, atiprasaṅgāt. tasmād asiddha-pratibandhasya hetor evâyaṃ doṣo, na dṛṣṭântasyêti. tathâpradarśita-vyatireka-viparīta-vyatirekāv api vaktum ayuktau, tayor vaktṛ-doṣatvāt. tathā hy: apradarśita-vyatirekas tair ukto, yathânityaḥ śabdaḥ, kṛtakatvād, ākāśavad iti. atra vidyamāno 'pi vyatireko vādinā vacanena nôdbhāvita iti duṣṭatā. viparīta-vyatirekaḥ punar abhihito, yathânityaḥ śabdaḥ, kṛtakatvād iti. atra vaidharmya-dṛṣṭânto: yad akṛtakaṃ tan nityaṃ bhavati, yathâkāśam iti. atra viparyasta-vyatireka-pradarśanād viparīta-vyatirekitvam. vaidharmya-prayoge hi sādhyâbhāvaḥ sādhanâbhāvâkrānto darśanīyo, na câievam atra, sādhanâbhāvasya sādhyâbhāva-vyāptatayâbhidhānād iti.
children.translated_text: Others have shown, through unreflecting speech, three additional fallacious examples, namely: non-exclusion (<s>avyatireka</s>), undemonstrated exclusion (<s>apradarśita-vyatireka</s>), and reversed exclusion (<s>viparīta-vyatireka</s>). These should not be presented by us, being unjustified. For: non-exclusion has been shown by them as follows: 'A certain person under discussion is not free from passion, because of being a speaker.' Here the negative-agreement example [is]: 'Whoever is free from passion is not a speaker, like a stone.' Although from the stone both [properties] are excluded, nevertheless, since exclusion through pervasion is not established, it is [called] non-exclusion. But this is unjustified to state, because non-exclusion is a defect of the reason. For if exclusion were established by the force of the example alone, then one lacking such capacity would justly be called a fallacious example; but this is not the case, because the example is adopted for the purpose of occasioning the recollection of the scope of the <s>pramāṇa</s> inclined toward grasping the previously existing connection. For it is not the case that [the exclusion] 'whatever is not observed in the absence of something does not exist in the absence of that thing' is established, apart from a <s>pramāṇa</s> grasping the invariable connection, in a single instance — because of over-extension. Therefore this is a defect of the reason alone, whose invariable connection is not established, not of the example. Likewise, undemonstrated exclusion and reversed exclusion are also unjustified to state, since both are defects of the speaker. For: undemonstrated exclusion has been stated by them as follows: 'Sound is non-eternal, because of being produced, like space.' Here, although the exclusion actually exists, it has not been brought out by the proponent's statement; hence the defect. Reversed exclusion, however, has been stated as follows: 'Sound is non-eternal, because of being produced.' Here the negative-agreement example [is]: 'Whatever is unproduced is eternal, like space.' Here, because the exclusion is shown in reverse, it is reversed exclusion. For in the negative-agreement formulation, the absence of the provable should be shown as pervaded by the absence of the prover; but here this is not so, because the absence of the prover is stated as pervaded by the absence of the provable.

children.text: vyatirekâpradarśanaṃ viparīta-vyatireka-pradarśanaṃ ca na vastuno doṣaḥ, kiṃ tarhi vacana-kuśalatā-vikalasyâbhidhāyakasya. kiṃ ca, yeṣāṃ bhavatām ado darśanaṃ: yad uta svârthânumāna-kāle svayaṃ hetu-darśana-mātrāt sādhya-pratīteḥ parârthânumānâvasare 'pi hetu-pratipādanam eva kartavyaṃ "viduṣāṃ vācyo hetur eva hi kevala" iti-vacanāt teṣāṃ ‘kṛtakatvād'; itîyatā hetûpanyāsenâiva sisādhayiṣita-sādhya-siddheḥ samasta-dṛṣṭântâbhāsa-varṇanam api pūrvâpara-vyāhata-vacana-racanā-cāturyam āvir-bhāvayati.āsātāṃ tāvad etau, dṛṣṭântasya sādhanâvayavatvenânabhyupagamāt. athêttham ācakṣīthā: anvaya-vyatirekâparijñāne pratipādyasya na dṛṣṭântam antareṇâitau darśayituṃ śakyāv, ato 'nvaya-vyatireka-darśanârthaṃ dṛṣṭânto 'bhidhātavyas, tataś ca tat-kāryâkāriṇāṃ tad-ābhāsatêti ced, gale gṛhītasyâyam ullāpas, tathâpy apradarśita-vyatireka-viparīta-vyatirekau dṛṣṭântâbhāsau na vāstavau, kiṃ tarhi vaktṛ-doṣa-samutthāv; ato nâbhidhātuṃ yuktau, tathā-vidhasya vidyamāna-vastu-prakāśana-sāmarthya-rahitasya nibiḍa-jaḍimâvaṣṭabdhasya puṃso vādânadhikāritvān, mātṛkā-pāṭha-śālā-yogyatayā viduṣāṃ vādayitum ayuktatvād iti.
children.translated_text: The non-demonstration of exclusion and the demonstration of reversed exclusion are not defects of the thing [i.e., the example] itself, but rather of the speaker who is deficient in skill of expression. Moreover, for those of you who hold this view — namely, that since at the time of <s>svārthānumāna</s> (inference for oneself) the apprehension of the provable arises from mere observation of the reason, therefore at the occasion of <s>parārthānumāna</s> (inference for the sake of others) too, only the reason need be stated, because of the dictum 'For the learned, the reason alone should be stated' — for such [as you], since the intended provable is established merely by the statement of the reason in 'because of being produced,' even the entire description of fallacious examples displays the ingenuity of self-contradictory verbal composition. But let these two [types] be set aside, since the example is not accepted [by us] as a component of the proof. Now if you were to say: 'When positive and negative concomitance are not known, these two [concomitances] cannot be shown to the person to be instructed without an example; therefore the example must be stated in order to demonstrate positive and negative concomitance; and consequently, those that fail to accomplish this are fallacious examples' — [we reply:] this is the protest of one who is already seized by the throat. Even so, the one with undemonstrated exclusion and the one with reversed exclusion are not genuine fallacious examples, but rather arise from defects of the speaker; therefore they are not justified to state, because a person of that kind — incapable of manifesting the existing reality, gripped by dense stupidity — is not qualified for debate, since it is unjustified to make the learned debate with one fit [only] for a primary school.

children.text: tad evaṃ parârthânumānaṃ vyācakṣāṇena yad uktaṃ -- yad uta "tat pakṣâdi-vacanâtmakam" iti -- tat pakṣa-hetu-dṛṣṭântānāṃ sâbhāsānāṃ pratipādanāt prāyaḥ paryantitaṃ; kevalaṃ tat parôkta-dūṣaṇôddhārād eva samīcīnatām ābibhartîty amunā prastāvena dūṣaṇaṃ sābhāsam abhidhātukāma āha:
children.translated_text: Thus, in explaining inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>), what was stated — namely, 'it consists of the statements of the thesis and the rest' — has been mostly completed through the exposition of the thesis, reason, and example together with their semblances. However, since it derives its correctness solely from the extraction of faults stated by the opponent, wishing to set forth refutation (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>) together with its semblance on this occasion, [the author] says:

children.text:
vādy-ukte sādhane prokta-doṣāṇām udbhāvanam /
  dūṣaṇaṃ niravadye tu dūṣaṇâbhāsa-nāmakam || 26 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> (refutation) is the exposing of faults stated in the proof adduced by the disputant; but when directed at a faultless [proof], it bears the name '<s>dūṣaṇābhāsa</s>' (semblance of refutation). (NA_26)
One whose nature is to speak —

children.text: ; sādhyate pratipādya-pratītāv āropyate 'numeyaṃ yena tat sādhanam. tac câneka-rūpaṃ prāk pratyapādi, tad yathā -- kvacid dhetur evâikaḥ, kvacit pakṣa-hetū, kvacit pakṣa-hetu-dṛṣṭântāḥ, kvacit ta eva sôpanayāḥ, kvacit sanigamanāḥ, kvacid ekâika-tac-chuddhi-vṛddhyêti, pratipādyasya kvacit kathañcit pratyāyayituṃ śakyatvāt, tat-pratyāyanôpāyasya ca sādhanatvād iti. tatrêha samyak-sādhanasya dūṣayitum aśakyatvāt, sādhanâbhāsa eva tat-sāmarthyôpapatteḥ, sādhanâbhāsam eva dūṣanôpanipātāt prāg avasthāyām anirjñātaṃ sāmānyena sādhana-dhvaninôktaṃ, tatra
children.translated_text: that by which the object to be inferred is proved — i.e., placed upon the cognition to be conveyed — is the proof. And this is of many forms, as was previously explained: sometimes the reason alone, sometimes the thesis and reason, sometimes the thesis, reason, and example, sometimes these same with the application, sometimes with the conclusion, sometimes with the purification of each one individually — since the object to be established can somehow be conveyed in each case, and whatever serves as a means to convey it is a proof. Herein, since a correct proof cannot be refuted — the capacity for refutation belonging only to a semblance of proof — what is referred to by the general term 'proof' in the state before the impact of refutation, being as yet unexamined, is actually a semblance of proof; in that,
— characterized by the presentation of a thesis contradicted by perception and the like, an unestablished reason and the like, and an example deficient in what is to be proved and the like —

children.text: prāśnikānāṃ purataḥ prakāśanaṃ yat tad dūṣyate svâbhipreta-sādhya-pratyāyana-vaikalya-lakṣaṇāṃ vikṛtiṃ nīyate sādhanam anenêti dūṣaṇam iti jñeyam.
children.translated_text: means making manifest before the examiners; that by which the proof is 'refuted' — i.e., brought to the state of deficiency characterized by failure to convey the intended object to be proved — is to be known as <s>dūṣaṇa</s> (refutation).
means departed, due to being correctly employed;
means evil, characterized by defects in the thesis and the like — that from which such wickedness is gone is

children.text: vādinôkta iti vartate. tathâpi matsaritayā pramṛdyôdaraṃ yad avidyamānānāṃ doṣāṇām udbhāvanaṃ tad dūṣaṇa-sthānôpanyastatvāt tat-kāryâkaraṇāt samyak-sādhane doṣôdbhāvanasya pralāpāyamānatvād dūṣaṇavadābhāsata iti
children.translated_text: 'stated by the disputant' is to be supplied. Nevertheless, out of jealousy, crushing one's own stomach [with envy], the exposing of non-existent faults — since it is presented in the place of refutation yet fails to accomplish the function of refutation, and since the exposing of faults in a correct proof amounts to mere prattle — it only appears to be refutation, and hence is

children.text: saṃjñā yasya tat-tathā. samartha-sādhanôpanyāsatvāt sādhite sādhye satām apy apaśabdâlaṅkārâdi-doṣāṇāṃ yad udbhāvanaṃ tad api
children.translated_text: — i.e., designation — and it is so called. Even the exposing of faults such as grammatical errors, stylistic defects, and the like, when the thesis has already been established through the presentation of a competent proof, is also

children.text: -śabdena viśeṣaṇârthena darśayati vastu-siddhy-arthaṃ vāda-pravṛttes, tasya siddhatvād, apaśabdâdīnām aprastutatayā tad-dvareṇa doṣa-prakāśanasyâsambaddha-pralāpa-rūpatvād, itarathā tāvan-mātreṇâiva parâpākaraṇa-siddheḥ samartha-sādhanânveṣaṇa-prayatno viśīryeta, prayojanâbhāvād iti.
children.translated_text: which serves as a qualifier, he shows that debate proceeds for the purpose of establishing reality; since that [reality] is already established [by the competent proof], and since faults such as grammatical errors are irrelevant and hence exposing faults through them amounts to incoherent prattle, otherwise the effort of seeking a competent proof would collapse on the mere ground of such [trivial objections], due to the absence of purpose.

children.text: tad evaṃ vyāvahārika-pramāṇasya pratyakṣa-parokṣa-svârtha-parârhâdi-bheda-bhinnasya lakṣaṇaṃ pratipādyâdhunā yaiḥ pāramārthikaṃ samastâvaraṇa-viccheda-labhyam aśeṣârtha-gocaraṃ kevala-jñānaṃ nâbhyupagamyate, tan-matôddalanârthaṃ tal-lakṣaṇam abhidhitsur āha:
children.translated_text: Thus, having explained the definition of conventional <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) with its divisions into perception and indirect knowledge, self-oriented and other-oriented, and so forth, now wishing to state the definition of [ultimate <s>pramāṇa</s>] — namely, <s>kevala-jñāna</s> (absolute cognition) which encompasses all objects and is obtained through the destruction of all obscurations — in order to refute the views of those who do not accept it, [the author] says:
That which shines forth as <s>kevala</s> (absolute), its nature being freed from all obscurations,
is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) — the constant manifestation of the nature of all objects. (NA_27)
means entire; that which covers or by which one is covered is

children.text: , tat-svarūpa-pracchādanaṃ karmêty arthaḥ, sakalaṃ ca tad avāraṇaṃ ca sakalâvaraṇaṃ, tena
children.translated_text: — meaning <s>karma</s> that conceals its true nature; 'all' and 'obscuration' combine as '<s>sakalāvaraṇa</s>'; from that,
means one whose own nature is such. Therefore,

children.text: asahāyam, āvaraṇa-kṣayôpaśama-vicitratayâiva bodhasya nānâkāratayā pravṛtteḥ, sāmastyena punar āvaraṇa-nirdalane vibandhaka-kāraṇa-vaikalyād ekâkāratayâiva tasya vivartanāt. ato jñānântara-nirapekṣaṃ
children.translated_text: means without companion — because when cognition operates in various forms due to the diversity of the destruction and subsidence of obscurations, but when all obscurations are completely destroyed, it operates in a single form due to the absence of any obstructing cause. Therefore, independent of any other cognition,

children.text: prathate nirupādhikaṃ dyotata ity arthaḥ, tat paramârthataḥ
children.translated_text: means that which manifests, that which illuminates without any limiting condition — that is, in the ultimate sense,
'whose nature is freed from all obscurations'
— having thus defined it through the door of its cause, and
— through its own nature, now defining it through the door of its effect, [the author] says:
means of all things in their true nature;
'constant manifestation of the nature of all objects' (<s>sakalārthātma-satata-pratibhāsanam</s>)

children.text: iti, pratibhāsyate 'nenêti pratibhāsanam, ātmano dharma-rūpatayā bhedavad-vivakṣitaṃ jñānam iti yāvat. asya ca pāramārthikatvaṃ, nirupacarita-śabdârthôpapatteḥ. tathā hy: akṣa-śabdo jīva-paryāyas, tataś câkṣaṃ prati vartata iti pratyakṣaṃ, yatrâtmanaḥ sākṣād vyāpāraḥ. vyāvahārikaṃ punar indriya-vyavahitâtma-vyāpāra-sampādyatvāt paramârthataḥ parokṣam eva: dhūmād agni-jñānavat, tiro-dhānâviśeṣāt.
children.translated_text: — thus; '<s>pratibhāsana</s>' means that by which things are manifested — i.e., cognition conceived as distinct from the self in the form of a property (<s>dharma</s>). And its being ultimate is established because the literal meaning of the word applies without figurative usage. For: the word '<s>akṣa</s>' is a synonym of <s>jīva</s> (soul), and therefore what operates directly with respect to the self (<s>akṣa</s>) is <s>pratyakṣa</s> — where there is the direct activity of the self. Conventional [perception], however, being accomplished through the activity of the self mediated by the sense organs, is in the ultimate sense actually indirect (<s>parokṣa</s>) — like the knowledge of fire from smoke, because there is no difference in [the fact of] concealment.

children.text: nanu ca prasiddhaṃ lakṣyam anūdyâprasiddhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vidhīyate -- sarvatrâyaṃ nyāyaḥ. aprasiddhe punar lakṣye lakṣaṇam abhidhīyamānam ambarâravindinī-kusuma-lakṣaṇavan nirgocaratāṃ yāyāt. tad idaṃ svarūpato 'prasādhya lakṣaṇam abhidadhānasya ko 'bhiprāya ity; atrôcyate -- ye ye mithyâvalepâdhmātântaḥ-karaṇāḥ pramāṇa-prasiddham apy adaḥ prati vipratipadyante, teṣāṃ dhy-āndhī-kṛta-buddhitvād avadhāraṇīyatām anena darśayati. kim asya pratipādakaṃ pramāṇam iti ced, ete brūmaḥ:
children.translated_text: Objection: The well-known definiendum is restated and the not-yet-known definition is predicated — this is the universal principle. But when a definition is predicated of an unestablished definiendum, it would be without any scope, like defining the flower of a sky-lotus. So what is the intention of one who predicates a definition without first establishing the definiendum's own nature? To this we reply: Those whose minds are inflated with the conceit of false views, who disagree even about what is established by <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) — since their intellects are blinded by obstinacy, he shows by this [verse] that it must be firmly ascertained. If you ask: what <s>pramāṇa</s> establishes this? — we respond:

children.text: samasti samasta-vastu-vistāra-gocaraṃ viśada-darśanaṃ, tad-gocarânumāna-pravṛtteḥ; iha yad-yad-gocaram anumānaṃ pravartate, tasya tasya grāhakaṃ kiñcit pratyakṣam udaya-padavīṃ samāsādayati, yathā citra-bhānoḥ; pravartate ca sakalârtha-viṣayam anumānam; atas tad-avalokinā viśada-darśanenâpi bhāvyam iti. sarvârtha-viṣayaṃ kim anumānaṃ pravartata iti ced, idam api brūma: iha yad yad asti tat tat sarvaṃ sthity-udayâpavarga-saṃsargam anubhavati, vastutvāt; yad yad vastu tat tat sthema-janma-pralayaiḥ kroḍī-kṛtaṃ; tad yathâṅgulir aṅgulitva-vakratva-rjutvâpekṣayêti; vastu ca yad asty, ataḥ prastuta-trayâkrāntaṃ tad avagantavyam. idam eva nikhilârtha-gocaram anekântânumānaṃ jñāna-kriyâbhyāsâtiśayān nikhilâvaraṇa-vicchede vibandhaka-kāraṇâbhāvād viśada-darśanī-bhavati. na cânumāna-pravṛttāv apy anarthitvâdinā pramātur apravṛttāv anumeya-gocara-pratyakṣâsambhavena vyabhicāraś codanīyaḥ, sambhavasya sādhyatayâbhipretatvāt. na ca sambhava-mātre 'sti vyabhicāraḥ, sarvânumeyānāṃ sambhavat-pratyakṣatayā vyāptatvād iti.
children.translated_text: There exists a clear vision (<s>viśada-darśana</s>) whose scope is the entire expanse of all objects — because inference operates with that as its scope. For: whatever object inference operates upon, there exists some perception that apprehends it and comes into being; just as with the multicolored sun. And inference does operate with respect to all objects; therefore, there must also be a clear vision that perceives them. If you ask: does inference really operate with respect to all objects? — we say this too: here, whatever exists, all of that undergoes the conjunction of persistence, origination, and destruction, because it is a real thing (<s>vastu</s>); whatever is a real thing is embraced by stability, birth, and dissolution, just as a finger, with respect to its finger-nature, curvedness, and straightness. And what exists is a real thing; therefore it must be understood as pervaded by this triad. This very inference concerning all objects — the <s>anekānta</s> (many-sided) inference — through the excellence of the practice of knowledge and action, in the [eventual] destruction of all obscurations, due to the absence of any obstructing cause, becomes clear vision. Nor should one object that there is a deviation [in the inference] because the cognizer may not engage due to lack of interest and so forth, and hence perception of the inferable object may not occur — for what is intended to be proved is precisely the possibility [of such cognition]. Nor is there any deviation in mere possibility, since all inferable objects are pervaded by the possibility of being perceived.

children.text: athavânyathânumānayāmaḥ: sambhavat-samasta-śuddhika ātmā, vidyamāna-śuddhy-upāyatvād; iha yo yo vidyamāna-śuddhy-upāyaḥ sa sa sambhavat-samasta-śuddhiko; yathā vidyamāna-kṣāra-mṛt-puṭa-pākâdi-śuddhy-upāyo ratna-viśeṣas, tathā ca vidyamāna-jñānâdy-abhyāsa-śuddhy-upāya ātmâtaḥ sambhavat-samasta-śuddhika iti. sāmastya-śuddhaś câtmā jñāna-jñāninoḥ kathañcid abhedāt kevalam abhidhīyata iti. jñānâdy-abhyāsaḥ kathaṃ viśuddhi-kāraṇam iti ced, āvaraṇa-mala-pratipakṣa-rūpatvād iti brūmaḥ. pratipakṣa-rūpatā katham avadhāritêiti cet, tavâiva darśanāt. tathā hi: dṛśyate jñānâdy-abhyāsataḥ pratikṣaṇam āvaraṇa-vilayo, viśiṣṭa-viśiṣṭatara-tat-kārya-bodhâdy-anubhavāt, tad-atiśaye punaḥ sāmastyôcchedaḥ syād ity abhidadhmahe. etena yat pare procur -- yathā: pratyakṣâdi-pramāṇa-pañcaka-gocarâtikrāntatvāt sarvârtha-saṃvedanam abhāvâkhya-ṣaṣṭha-pramāṇa-gocaratāṃ pratipadyate -- tad ayuktaṃ, tat-sambhavasyânumānena pratipādanāt, pramāṇa-pañcaka-pravartanâbhāvâsiddheḥ. kiṃ ca, pramāṇa-pañcakaṃ tad-gocaraṃ na pravartata iti kathaṃ bhavato nirṇayaḥ? kiṃ niyata-deśa-kāla-vyāptyā yad vā samasta-deśa-kālâskandanenêti? yady ādyaḥ pakṣas, tato yathā ghaṭâdeḥ kvacit pramāṇa-pañcakaṃ tad-gocaraṃ nirvartamānam abhāvaṃ sādhayaty, evaṃ samasta-vastu-saṃvedana-gocaram api tan nivartamānaṃ niyata-deśa-daśâvacchinnam abhāvaṃ sādhayen, na sarvatra; tataś ca ghaṭâdivat tad durnivāraṃ syāt. atha dvitīyaḥ pakṣo, 'sāv asambhavy eva; samasta-deśa-kāla-varti-puruṣa-pariṣat-saṃvedana-sākṣāt-kāriṇo hy evaṃ vaktuṃ yuktaṃ, yad uta na kvacit samastârtha-saṃvedanaṃ astîti -- na bhavatas, tathā-vidha-puruṣa-sambhavânabhyupagamāt. itarathā ya eva kaścin niścityâivam abhidadhyāt, sa eva samasta-vastu-vistāra-vyāpi-jñānâloka iti samastârtha-gocara-saṃvedana-siddhir ity āstāṃ tāvat.
children.translated_text: Alternatively, we infer thus: the self (<s>ātman</s>) is one in which complete purification is possible, because it possesses existing means of purification. Here, whatever possesses existing means of purification is one in which complete purification is possible; just as a particular gem possesses existing means of purification such as alkali, clay, and smelting; and similarly, the self possesses existing means of purification such as the practice of knowledge; therefore, complete purification is possible in it. And the self, when completely purified, is called <s>kevala</s> (absolute), because there is in some sense non-difference between knowledge and the knower. If you ask: how is the practice of knowledge and the like a cause of purification? — we say: because it is of the nature of a counteragent to the impurity of obscuration. If you ask: how is the nature of a counteragent ascertained? — from your own observation. For it is observed that through the practice of knowledge and the like, there is a dissolution of obscuration at every moment, as experienced through progressively more distinguished and even more distinguished cognition and other effects; when this reaches its culmination, there would be complete destruction [of obscuration] — this is what we maintain. By this, what others have proclaimed — namely, that since the cognition of all objects transcends the scope of the five <s>pramāṇas</s> such as perception and the rest, it falls within the scope of a sixth <s>pramāṇa</s> called non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>) — that is unjustified, because its possibility is established by inference, and because the non-operation of the five <s>pramāṇas</s> [in that domain] is itself unestablished. Moreover, how is it your conclusion that the five <s>pramāṇas</s> do not operate with respect to that? Is it by their pervading a limited range of place and time, or by their failing to encompass all places and times? If the first alternative, then just as the five <s>pramāṇas</s> operating with respect to a pot and the like in a particular domain establish the non-existence [of the pot elsewhere], so too their non-operation with respect to the cognition of all objects, being limited to a particular place and circumstance, would establish non-existence only there, not everywhere; and in that case, like a pot, it would be impossible to prevent [its existence]. If the second alternative, that is simply impossible; for only one who directly perceives the awareness of all persons in all places and times would be justified in saying 'nowhere does the cognition of all objects exist' — not you, since you do not accept the possibility of such a person. Otherwise, whoever would ascertain and declare this would himself be a light of knowledge pervading the entire expanse of all objects — and thus the existence of cognition encompassing all objects would be established. But let that be for now.

children.text: tad evaṃ pramāṇa-viṣaye lakṣaṇa-saṃkhyā-vipratipattī nirākṛtyâdhunā krama-prāptāṃ gocara-vipratipattiṃ bahu-vaktavyatvād anirākṛtya tāvat phala-vipratipattiṃ nirācikīrṣur āha:
children.translated_text: Thus, having refuted the disagreements regarding definition and enumeration in the domain of <s>pramāṇa</s>, now, without refuting the disagreement regarding the object — since there is much to be said about it — wishing to resolve the disagreement regarding the result, [the author] says:
The direct result of <s>pramāṇa</s> is the removal of ignorance;
for <s>kevala</s> (absolute cognition), bliss and equanimity; for the rest, the understanding of what to adopt and what to avoid. (NA_28)

children.text: : sākṣād asākṣāc cânantaraṃ vyavahitaṃ cêty arthaḥ. tatra
children.translated_text: — direct and indirect, i.e., immediate and remote. Therein,
means non-determination, the failure to delimit the object to be known; its

children.text: , ajñānôddalana-dvāreṇa tasya pravṛttes, tasya ca sarvânartha-mūlatayā pramātr-apakāritvāt. tan-nivartanasya prayojanatā yuktâiva. etac cânantara-prayojanaṃ sarva-jñānānām eka-rūpatvāt sāmānyenôktam. vyavahita-prayojanaṃ punar vibhāgenâha:
children.translated_text: because <s>pramāṇa</s> operates through the destruction of ignorance, and because ignorance, being the root of all misfortune, is harmful to the cognizer. Therefore the removal of ignorance is justifiably the purpose [of <s>pramāṇa</s>]. This immediate purpose is stated in general terms, since it is the same for all cognitions. The remote purpose, however, he states with a distinction:
means of the cognition of the omniscient one;
means the experience of supreme joy transcending worldly sensory pleasure;
means a state of neutrality due to the absence of any desire for adoption or avoidance even while directly experiencing all objects; these
are the result — this is the meaning.
means of the ordinary worldly <s>pramāṇa</s>, which is other than that [absolute cognition];
means abandonment; of those two, adoption and avoidance —

children.text: , sā phalam iti yāvat. tataś câdeyānāṃ samyag-darśanâdi-srak-candanâdīnāṃ yâditsā, tathā heyānāṃ mithyā-darśanâdi-viṣa-kaṇṭakâdīnāṃ yā jihāsā sā pramāṇa-sādhyâpramāṇāt tad-asiddheḥ, prekṣā-pūrva-kāriṇāṃ tataḥ pravṛtty-ayogād ity uktaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: , that is the result. And from that, the desire to acquire things worthy of acceptance such as <s>samyag-darśana</s> (right faith) and the like, garlands, sandalwood, and so forth, and likewise the desire to avoid things worthy of rejection such as <s>mithyā-darśana</s> (false faith) and the like, poison, thorns, and so forth — that [desire] is not established without a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge), because the object to be established by a <s>pramāṇa</s> cannot be established without it; for those who act deliberately, purposeful activity would be impossible without it — this is what is stated.
Now he explains the disagreement regarding the object-domain:
A thing whose nature is <s>anekānta</s> (many-sided) is the object-domain of all cognitions;
an object qualified by one aspect is considered the domain of a <s>naya</s> (standpoint). (NA_29)
essential forms of which [are many] — that is

children.text: samasta-saṃvittīnām. anenânekântam antareṇa saṃvedana-prasara-vyavacchedaṃ darśayati, bhrānta-saṃvedanānām apy anekântôddyotana-paṭiṣṭhatayā pravṛtteḥ, kevalaṃ keṣucid aṃśeṣu visaṃvādakatvād apramāṇāni tāni saṅgīryante. tad ayam abhiprāyo: yadā saṃvedana-sāmānyam apy anekânta-viraheṇa na pravartitum utsahate, tadā tad-viśeṣa-bhūtaṃ pramāṇam ekânte pravartiṣyata iti dūrâpāstâvakāśâivâiṣā vārtā, tathâpy anādi-mithyâbhiniveśa-vāsitântaḥ-karaṇāḥ kudarśana-vipralabdha-buddhayo bahavo 'tra vipratipadyanta iti sarva-pramāṇānām anekânta-gocaratva-sādhakaṃ pramāṇam abhidhīyate: iha yat pramāṇaṃ tat parasparâvinirluṭhitâneka-dharma-parikarita-vastuno grāhakaṃ, tasyâiva tatra pratibhāsamānatvād; iha yad yatra pratibhāti, tad eva tad-gocaratayâbhyupagantavyaṃ; tad -- yathā nirādīnava-nayana-prabhava-darśane pratibhāsamānaṃ pāṭalatayā japā-kusumaṃ tathâiva tad-gocaratayâbhyupagamyate; parasparâvibhaktâneka-svabhāvâkrānta-mūrtikaṃ ca bahir antaś ca vastu sarva-pramāṇeṣu prathata ity; atas tad eva teṣāṃ gocaraḥ.
children.translated_text: of the totality of awarenesses. By this he shows that without <s>anekānta</s> (many-sidedness), the operation of cognition would be cut off, because even erroneous cognitions proceed on the basis of the illumination of <s>anekānta</s>, and they are declared non-<s>pramāṇa</s> only because they are misleading with respect to certain aspects. The purport is this: when even cognition in general is unable to operate without <s>anekānta</s>, then the claim that <s>pramāṇa</s>, which is a particular form of cognition, will operate with respect to a single exclusive aspect — this is a matter whose scope is utterly remote. Nevertheless, many whose inner faculties are perfumed by beginningless attachment to false views, whose intellects are deceived by wrong philosophies, disagree about this. Therefore a <s>pramāṇa</s> establishing that the object-domain of all <s>pramāṇas</s> is <s>anekānta</s> is stated: here, whatever is a <s>pramāṇa</s> grasps a thing endowed with many properties not mutually negated, because it is precisely that which appears therein; here, whatever appears in whatever [cognition], that alone is to be accepted as its object-domain; thus — just as a <s>japā</s>-flower (hibiscus), appearing as red in a perception arising from an unimpaired eye, is accepted as the object-domain of just that [perception]; and a thing whose form is pervaded by many mutually undivided natures, both external and internal, manifests in all <s>pramāṇas</s>; therefore that alone is their object-domain.

children.text: -śiṣyakais tāvad asya hetor asiddhatâdi-doṣaḥ pratipādayituṃ śakyas, tad-abhyupagamam antareṇa svâbhipreta-vastuno 'vasthānâbhāvāt. tathā hy: ekasmin dharmiṇi bahavo dharmās tato bhinna-tanavaḥ kathaṃ varteran? bhedâviśeṣeṇa sarvatra tad-vṛtti-prasaṅgāt. tatrâiva teṣāṃ samavāyān nânyatra vartanta iti cen, nanu so 'pi samavāyo yady upakāryôpakāraka-bhāva-vyatirekeṇâpi bhavati, tataḥ sarvatrâviśeṣeṇa prasajyeta, tad-abhāvâviśeṣāt. asty evôpakāryôpakāraka-bhāva iti ced, hanta hato 'sy, anekôpakārakasyâneka-svabhāvatā-prāptes, tad-virahe 'nekôpakārakatvâbhāvāt. na hi yena svabhāvenâikasyôpakaroti tenâiva dvitīyasya, tasya tatrâivôpayuktatvād, dvitīyôpakāraka-svabhāvasya tad-upamardana-dvāreṇôtpatter, itarathâikam evôpakurvaṃs tiṣṭhet, tad-eka-svabhāvāt. bhinnābhiḥ śaktibhir upakaroti, na bhinnaiḥ svabhāvais, tena nânekânta iti cet, tās tarhi tatra kathaṃ vartanta iti vācyam. samavāyād ity-uttare 'sāv apy upakāryôpakāraka-bhāvam antareṇa kathaṃ na sarvatrêti prācīnaṃ codyaṃ paścāl-lagnam anudhāvati. upakāryôpakāraka-bhāvâbhyupagame punar apy aneka-svabhāvatā-pradarśita-yukteḥ punaḥ śakty-upakāraka-bhinna-śakti-parikalpane tad evâvartate, tan na bhinna-dharma-parikalpane 'py anekântān mokṣa iti varam ādāv eva matsaritāṃ vihāyâneka-dharmâdhyāsitaṃ vastv abhyupagatam. kiṃ bheda-kalpanayâsthāna evâtmanā parikleśitenêti. kiṃ cânekântâbhyupagame saty eṣa guṇaḥ: paraspara-vibhakteṣu saṃyogi-saṃyoga-samavāyi-samavāya-guṇa-guṇy-avayavâvayavi-vyakti-sāmānyâdiṣu saṃyoga-samavāya-guṇy-avayavi-sāmānyâdīnāṃ saṃyogi-samavāyi-guṇâvayava-viśeṣâdiṣu vartana-cintāyāṃ yad dūṣaṇa-jālam upanipatati, tad api parihṛtaṃ bhavaty, ekânta-bheda eva tad-upapatter, anekânte tad-utthānâbhāvāt. tathā hi: bhinnāḥ khalu saṃyogâdayaḥ saṃyogy-ādibhyo vikalpayituṃ pāryante -- yad uta katham eta eteṣu vartanta iti? kim eka-deśena yad vā sāmastyena? yady eka-deśena, tad ayuktaṃ, teṣāṃ niravayavatvâbhyupagamāt. sâvayavatve 'pi tebhyo 'vayavebhyo yady abhinnās, tato 'nekântâpattir, ekasyânekâvayavatva-prāpteḥ. atha bhinnās teṣv api te kathaṃ vartanta ity vācyam: eka-deśena sāmastyena vā. eka-deśa-pakṣe tad evâvartata ity anavasthā. atha sāmastyena, tad apy asādhīyaḥ, pratyekaṃ parisamāptatayā saṃyogâdi-bahutva-prasaṅgāt. tad-abhinnāḥ punaḥ saṃyogâdayo na vikalpa-bhājo bhavanti. abheda-pakṣe 'pi saṃyogâdi-mātraṃ saṃyogy-ādi-mātraṃ vā syād iti cen, na, tasyâpy ekântenânabhyupagamāt, kiṃ tarhy anyonyâviśliṣṭa-svarūpā vivakṣayā sandarśanīya-bhedāḥ sarva evâite 'bhyupagamyante, tathā-vidhānāṃ kuyukti-vikalpôtthāpita-dūṣaṇa-samūha-nirākaraṇa-kṣamatvād, abādhita-pratibhāseṣu sarvatra teṣāṃ tathâiva pratibhāsanād, anyathā pratibhāsamānānām anyathā parikalpane dṛṣṭa-hāny-adṛṣṭa-parikalpanā-dvāreṇâsamañjasa-prāptes; tathā ca
children.translated_text: who maintain the distinction of <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) and <s>dharma</s> (property) as mutually separated — by them, the fault of unestablishedness and so forth of this reason cannot be demonstrated, because without accepting that [<s>anekānta</s>], the status of the thing they themselves intend could not be maintained. For consider: how could many properties, having natures distinct from it, subsist in a single property-bearer? Because in the absence of any difference [in the relation], there would be the absurd consequence of their occurrence everywhere. If [you say] they do not occur elsewhere because of their <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) in that very [property-bearer] — but then, if that <s>samavāya</s> too obtains even without the relation of that which is to be benefited and that which benefits, then it would absurdly apply everywhere without distinction, since there is no difference in the absence of that [relation]. If [you say] the relation of benefited-and-benefiter does exist — well then, you are defeated, because a thing with many benefiters would thereby attain a many-natured character, and in the absence of that [relation], there would be no state of having many benefiters. For it is not the case that by the very nature by which it benefits one thing, it benefits a second, since that [nature] is exhausted in that very [first benefiting]; the nature that benefits the second arises through the suppression of that [first nature], for otherwise it would remain benefiting only one, due to its having a single nature. If [you say] it benefits by distinct capacities (<s>śaktis</s>), not by distinct natures, and therefore there is no <s>anekānta</s> — then it must be said: how do those [capacities] subsist in that [thing]? If the reply is 'by <s>samavāya</s> (inherence),' even that [<s>samavāya</s>] — how is it not everywhere without the relation of benefited-and-benefiter? — the earlier objection follows closely behind as a later one. And upon accepting the relation of benefited-and-benefiter, since the reasoning demonstrating many-naturedness has been shown again, and since in the further postulation of distinct capacities benefiting the capacities, the same [regress] recurs — therefore there is no escape from <s>anekānta</s> even in the postulation of distinct properties. It is better to abandon stinginess from the very beginning and accept the thing as invested with many properties. Why should one torment oneself by fabricating distinctions in the wrong place? Moreover, in accepting <s>anekānta</s>, there is this advantage: in the contemplation of how, among mutually separated [categories such as] <s>saṃyogin</s> (conjunct) and <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), <s>samavāyin</s> (inherent) and <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), <s>guṇa</s> (quality) and <s>guṇin</s> (quality-bearer), <s>avayava</s> (part) and <s>avayavin</s> (whole), <s>vyakti</s> (particular) and <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), etc. — how <s>saṃyoga</s>, <s>samavāya</s>, quality-bearer, whole, universal, and the like subsist in conjuncts, inherents, qualities, parts, particulars, and the like — the net of objections that descends is also resolved, because those [objections] are established only on the basis of absolute distinction, and do not arise in <s>anekānta</s>. For consider: distinct as they are, conjunction and the like can be imagined as separate from conjuncts and the like — namely, how do they subsist in them? Is it by one part, or by the whole? If by one part — that is untenable, because they are accepted as partless. Even if they have parts, if those parts are non-distinct from them, then <s>anekānta</s> would follow, since one thing would attain the character of having many parts. If distinct, then it must be said: how do they subsist in those [parts] too? By one part or by the whole? In the position of one part, the same [regress] recurs — hence an infinite regress. If by the whole — that too is worse, because since each [part] is complete in itself, there would be the absurd consequence of a multiplicity of conjunctions and the like. When non-distinct from them, conjunction and the like are not subject to conceptual differentiation. If [you say] that even in the position of non-distinction, it would be either mere conjunction etc. or mere conjunct etc. — no, because that too is not accepted on the basis of a single exclusive [aspect]; rather, all of these are accepted as having natures mutually inseparable, with distinctions to be displayed according to the intention of what is to be expressed, because such [entities] are capable of removing the mass of objections raised by the conceptual fabrications of bad reasoning, because in all unsublated appearances they appear in precisely that way, and because in construing what appears one way as being otherwise, there would result the incoherence of abandoning the observed and fabricating the unobserved. And thus
and the like would be established — because there would be no distinguishing feature [to prevent it].
By this, those of this reason [who are]

children.text: apy asiddhatâdi-doṣam abhidhitsavo maukyam ānītāḥ. tathā hy: antar ekaṃ saṃvedanam aparâpara-harṣa-viṣādâdy-ananta-dharma-vivartâkrānta-rūpaṃ bahiś ca ghaṭâdikam arthaṃ nava-purāṇâdi-vartula-pārthivatvâdy-aneka-svabhāvâvaṣṭabdha-śarīraṃ sākṣāl lakṣayantaḥ kathaṃ tad-viparīta-kathane pravarteran? prakṛti-puruṣâtmakaṃ dravyam evâikaṃ tāttvikaṃ, paryāya-bhrānti-janakaḥ punar vivarto 'pāramārthika iti cen, na, dvayor api sarva-pramāṇeṣu prakāśamānayor abādhitayoḥ sarva-vyavahāra-nibandhanayoḥ pakṣa-pātam antareṇâikasya nihnotum aśakyatvāt. tathā sati vivarta eva tāttviko, dravyaṃ punar alīkam iti paryāya-pakṣa-pātī prasañjayan durniṣedhaḥ syād iti. athêttham abhidadhīthā: dravyaṃ sarvatrâvyabhicarita-rūpatvāt satyaṃ, paryāyāḥ punar vyabhicāriṇa ity asatyāḥ, tad ayuktam. yadi nāma dravyam abheda-rūpatvāt sarvatrânuvartate, paryāyās tu bheda-rūpatvād vyavacchidyante, tathâpi tat satyam, itare 'līkā iti vaktuṃ na pāryate, na hi nīlaṃ pīta-rūpatāṃ na bibhartîty-etāvatā tad asatyam, atiprasaṅgāt, sarvasya para-rūpa-parihārâvasthāyitayâlīkatva-prāpteḥ. atha dravyam eva paryāyās, tad-avyatiriktatvāt, tat-svarūpavan, na santi vā dravya-vyatirekiṇaḥ paryāyā, niḥsvabhāvatvāt, kha-puṣpavad iti pramāṇayasi, tathā sati paryāyā eva dravyaṃ, tad-avyatiriktatvāt tat-svarūpavan, nâsti vā paryāya-vyatiriktaṃ dravyaṃ, niṣparyāyatvād, ākāśa-kusumavad itîtaro 'pi pramāṇayan kena vāryeta. tan na pakṣa-dvaye 'pi kācid viśeṣôpalabdhir iti. yathâivânanta-saha-krama-varti-paryāyâdhyāsitaṃ vastu sarva-pramāṇeṣu prakāśate tathâivâbhyupagantavyaṃ, tathā cânyasyâbhāvāt tad eva tad-gocara iti sthitam.
children.translated_text: too, wishing to demonstrate the fault of unestablishedness and the like, are reduced to silence. For consider: directly perceiving internally a single awareness whose form is pervaded by the transformations of innumerable properties such as successive joy, sorrow, and the like, and externally an object such as a pot endowed with a body sustained by many natures such as new, old, round, earthen, etc. — how could they proceed to assert the opposite of that? If [you say] only substance (<s>dravya</s>) consisting of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness) is the single reality, while transformation (<s>vivarta</s>) that generates the illusion of modes is non-ultimate — no, because since both [substance and mode] are manifest in all <s>pramāṇas</s>, are unsublated, and are the basis of all practical activity, it is impossible to deny one without partiality. In that case, one taking the side of modes would generate the irrefutable [counter-thesis] that transformation alone is real while substance is unreal. Now, if you were to say this: substance is real because its form is invariable everywhere, while modes, being variable, are unreal — that is untenable. Even if substance, being of the nature of non-difference, continues everywhere, while modes, being of the nature of difference, are delimited — still, one cannot say that substance is real and the others are unreal. For it is not the case that because blue does not bear the form of yellow, it is therefore unreal — that would be an over-extension, since everything, being in the condition of excluding the form of another, would turn out to be unreal. Now, if you reason that modes are just substance, being non-different from it, and have the nature of substance; or that there are no modes different from substance, because they are devoid of own-nature, like a sky-flower — in that case, the other [party] too, reasoning that substance is just the modes, being non-different from them, and has the nature of modes; or that there is no substance different from modes, because it is without modes, like a sky-flower — by what could he be prevented? Therefore in neither position is any distinguishing feature found. Just as a thing invested with modes subsisting simultaneously and successively without limit appears in all <s>pramāṇas</s>, so it should be accepted; and since there is nothing else, that alone is their object-domain — this is established.
also, among those who follow that doctrine,

children.text: tāvad asya hetor asiddhatām āvir-bhāvayituṃ nôtsahate, tad-abhyupagati-vyatirekeṇa nija-darśana-vyavasthânupapatteḥ. tathā hi: bahis tāvad ekaṃ kāraṇam aparâpara-sāmagry-antaḥ-pātitayâneka-kārya-kāryāvedyate, yathā rūpaṃ svôttara-kṣaṇaṃ svâvagāhi-jñānâdikaṃ ca yugapaj janayati. yadi câika-kṣaṇa-vartinaḥ sāmagrī-bhedena bhedam anubhavata eva bhinna-deśa-nānā-kārya-kāritā, tathā sati nitya-pakṣôditaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ sva-mastakôpanipāti syāt, tasyâpi tathâiva bhinna-kāla-kārya-nirvartane 'pi bhedâbhāva-prasaṅgāt. tathā pratibhāsa-bhedena kṣaṇa-kṣayi-rūpâdi-svalakṣaṇa-vilakṣaṇatvâbhyupagamaś câivaṃ nirnibandhanaḥ syāt, kauṭasthyam ābibhrato 'pi dravyasyâparâpara-kāraṇa-kalāpântar-gatatayā nava-purāṇâdi-paryāya-rūpa-rasa-gandha-sparśâvabhāsa-lakṣaṇa-kārya-sampādanâvirodha-prasakteḥ. kiṃ câyam ekaṃ svâvayava-vyāpinaṃ kālântara-saṃcariṣṇum ākāraṃ sākṣāl lakṣayan kṣaṇa-kṣayi-paramâṇu-lakṣaṇāni svalakṣaṇāny ācakṣīta nânyathā, yathâkūtaṃ tad-avabhāsasya svapnântare 'py anupalakṣaṇāl; lakṣitasya câlakṣita-vyatireka-nirākaraṇatas tādātmyaṃ kathayan sva-girânekântâvabhāsaṃ samarthayate. tathā hy: alakṣita-paramâṇu-pārimāṇḍalya-pratikṣaṇa-vivartam api svalakṣaṇaṃ sthira-sthūrâdy-ātmanā darśayati svarūpam, anyathā suṣuptaṃ jagad āsajyeta, tad-aprakāśane pramāṇântarasyâpy atyanta-vilakṣaṇa-svalakṣaṇâvedakasyâpravṛtti-prasaṅgāt. tathântaḥ-saṃvedanam artha-svarūpâpekṣayā bahir-mukhântar-mukha-savikalpâvikalpa-bhrāntâbhrāntâdi-pratibhāsam ekam abhyupayataḥ katham anekântâvabhāso 'siddhaḥ syāt? tathā nānā-deśa-sthitârtha-sārtha-samarpitâkārôparaktam ekam ākāra-bhede 'py anyathā yugapat-prakāśamāna-sitâsitâdy-artha-vyavasthity-anupapatteḥ saṃvedanam anumanyamānaḥ kathaṃ bhinna-samaya-bhāvi-harṣa-viṣādâdy-aneka-vivarta-vaśāt tad-bhedam ātyantikam abhidadhīta, abhinna-yoga-kṣematvād. yugapad-bhāvināṃ saṃvid-antar-niviṣṭâkārāṇām ekatvaṃ na harṣâdīnāṃ, tad-viparyayād iti cen, na, tat-sāmarthya-vyavasthāpyârthâbheda-prasaṅgāt, tad-ekatayā sita-pītâdiṣu jñānasya bodha-rūpeṇâivâviśiṣṭatvāt. tad evaṃ bahir antaś câikâneka-rūpatve pramāṇataḥ sthiteḥ svalakṣaṇasyânyathā svâbhyupeta-darśana-vyavasthâyogān nârtha-vādy anekânta-prakāśaṃ pratikṣeptum arhati.
children.translated_text: at least are unable to make manifest the unestablishedness of this reason, because without accepting that [<s>anekānta</s>], the establishment of their own philosophical system would be impossible. For consider: externally, a single cause, being included within successive assemblages of conditions, is known to produce many effects — just as form simultaneously produces its own next moment and a cognition that apprehends it, and so forth. And if [the cause], existing in a single moment, experiences differentiation through the difference of [causal] assemblages such that it produces diverse effects in different places — in that case, the objection raised against the position of permanence would fall upon their own heads, since even for that [permanent entity], in producing effects at different times, the absurd consequence of non-difference [from the momentary] would follow. Likewise, the acceptance that [an entity is] different from the momentary <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (own-characteristic) of perishing-in-an-instant form and the like, on the basis of difference in appearance, would thus be without foundation, because even for a substance that maintains its unchanging character, being included within successive assemblages of causes, the non-contradiction of producing effects characterized by appearances of new, old, and other modal forms of color, taste, smell, and touch would follow. Moreover, this [person], directly perceiving a form that pervades its own parts, persists across time, and is unitary — would he call [those] <s>svalakṣaṇas</s> (own-characteristics) characterized by atoms perishing in an instant, and not otherwise? — since even in a dream the appearance of that [unitary form] is not unperceived, as is well-known; and since, by declaring the identity of what is perceived with what is not perceived, he by his own words supports the appearance of <s>anekānta</s>. For consider: a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, though it is a transformation of unperceived atomic sphericity perishing at every instant, displays its own nature in the form of stable, gross, etc.; otherwise the world would be as if in deep sleep, since even another <s>pramāṇa</s> — being unable to reveal an utterly different <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> — would fail to operate. Likewise, for one who accepts that internal awareness, which is singular, appears as outward-facing, inward-facing, determinate, indeterminate, erroneous, non-erroneous, etc., relative to the nature of objects — how could the appearance of <s>anekānta</s> be unestablished? Likewise, for one who accepts that awareness is singular even in difference of form — because it is tinged with the forms presented by a multitude of objects situated in various places, and because otherwise the [simultaneous] determination of white, dark, and other objects manifesting simultaneously could not be coherently explained — how could one declare its difference to be absolute on account of the many transformations of joy, sorrow, etc. occurring at different times, since their welfare and adversity are non-different? If [you say] the unity belongs to the forms of awareness situated within cognition that are simultaneous, not to joy and the like, because the reverse [obtains for them] — no, because there would be the absurd consequence of non-difference of objects established through the capacity of those [simultaneous forms], since by virtue of their unity, knowledge would be indistinguishable in its cognitive nature with respect to white, yellow, and the like. Thus, since the one-and-many nature both externally and internally is established from <s>pramāṇa</s>, the proponent of [external] objects (<s>arthavādin</s>) — because the establishment of his own accepted system would otherwise be impossible — should not reject the appearance of <s>anekānta</s> in <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>.
Likewise, even the doctrine that has embraced

children.text: -matam api balād anekânta-prakāśa-rajjur āveṣṭayaty, ekasyâpi jñānasyâneka-vedya-vedakâkāratayā prathanôpagateḥ. eka-yoga-kṣematvāt tad-aikyam iti cen, na, yugapad-udaya-pralayavatāṃ saha-vedināṃ sakala-santānānām ekatva-prasaṅgāt. saṃvṛti-darśitatvād anekatvasya, na tena sva-saṃvedana-sākṣāt-kṛta-pāramārthikâikatva-kṣatir iti cen, na,
children.translated_text: thought is forcibly bound by the rope of the appearance of <s>anekānta</s>, because even a single cognition is accepted as manifesting with multiple forms of known and knower. If [you say] their unity is due to their having one welfare — no, because there would be the absurd consequence that all continua of co-experiencers who arise and perish simultaneously would be one. If [you say] that the multiplicity is shown from the conventional perspective (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), and therefore there is no impairment of the ultimate unity directly realized by <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) — no,
because there would be the absurd consequence of the inability to refute the doctrine of the <s>Brahmavādins</s> (Vedāntins),

children.text: -matâpratiṣedha-prasakter, yato 'nādy-avidyā-balād ekam akramaṃ sacetanaṃ sva-saṃvedana-sākṣāt-kṛtam api brahmânekaṃ kramavac cetanâcetanaṃ parokṣâparokṣaṃ lakṣyate, bhavat-parikalpita-grāhya-grāhakâkāra-vivikta-saṃvedanavad iti tenâpi na durupapādam. astu vâyam anekântâvabhāso bhrāntas, tathâpi saṃvedanasyâdvayatā na lakṣyate, tal-lakṣaṇe sakalâsumatām adhunâiva muktatâvāpteḥ. lakṣyate ca tat kathañcid, itarathā suṣupta-daśāvat sarva-vyavahārôccheda-prasaṅgād ity ekasyâpi saṃvedanasya lakṣitâlakṣitatvenânekânta-pratibhāso duḥśako 'pahnotum iti
children.translated_text: since [they could say that] by the power of beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), the one, non-sequential, conscious <s>Brahman</s>, though directly realized by self-awareness, is perceived as many, sequential, conscious-and-unconscious, mediate-and-immediate — just like the awareness devoid of the forms of grasped and grasper that you [Yogācāras] postulate — and that too would not be difficult to establish. Or let this appearance of <s>anekānta</s> be erroneous; even so, the non-duality of awareness is not perceived, since if it were perceived in its [complete] definition, all the unfortunate [non-Jain thinkers] would attain liberation this very moment. And it is perceived in some manner, for otherwise — as in the state of deep sleep — there would be the absurd consequence of the cessation of all practical activity. Therefore, even for a single awareness, the appearance of <s>anekānta</s> through its being both perceived and unperceived is difficult to deny. Thus

children.text: apy asya hetor asiddhatâvir-bhāvanaṃ prati tūṣṇīm āsīta.
children.translated_text: should remain silent regarding the attempt to make manifest the unestablishedness of this reason.

children.text: samastâbhāvād asiddho 'nekânta-prakāśa iti cen, na, tasyâpi pramāṇa-prameyâbhāve na sarvâbhāvâvedanaṃ samasty, anyathâpramāṇakaṃ sarvaṃ sarvatra vidyata iti parasyâpi vadato na vadana-bhaṅgaḥ syāt, tad-abhyupagame 'bhyupagama-kṣatiḥ. tayoś ca darśitavad anekânta-prakāśa iti nâsiddho hetuḥ. maru-marīcikā-nicaya-cumbini saṃvedane jalôllekhe 'pi tad-gocaratvâbhyupagamâbhāvād anaikāntiko 'yam iti mā śaṅkiṣṭhās, tasya bhrāntatvād, abhrānta-prakāśo hi tad-abhyupagati-hetuḥ. athâyam apîtarêtara-vinirluṭhita-paramâṇu-kṣaṇa-kṣayi-bodhena bādhyamānatvād bhrānta ity ācakṣīthās, tad ayuktaṃ, yatas tad-bodhaḥ kim upalabdhi-mātram yad vā nirṇayaḥ? yady ādyaḥ kalpas tadânumānaṃ viśīryeta, nirgocaratvāt, prāthamakalpikenâiva nirvikalpaka-vivikta-darśanena virodha-bhīrutayā sarvathā vastu-grahaṇâbhyupagamāt, pramāṇa-kalite ca mānântara-vaiyarthyād, anavasthā-prāpteḥ. atha dvitīyas, tathā sati sarvaṃ nirvikalpakam apramāṇatām aśnuvīta. na ca nirṇayo 'nekânta-prakāśaṃ bādhate, 'pi tu samarthayate, bahir antaś ca tathâiva tad-vijṛmbhaṇāt. atha sarvathā vastu-grahaṇe 'pi nirvikalpakaṃ yatrâṃśe pāścātyaṃ vyavahāra-kāri-vyavasāyam upajanayati, tatrâiva pramāṇatām āskandati nânyatrêti manyethās, tathā sati yad-anantaram artha-kriyā-samarthârtha-prārthanayā puruṣaḥ pravartate sa eva nirṇayaḥ prāmāṇyaṃ svī-kuryān, na nirvikalpakaṃ, taj-janakatve 'pi sannikarṣâdivad ity āsajyeta. nirvikalpakam anadhigatârthâdhigantṛtvāt pramāṇaṃ, na vyavasitis, tad-vikalpatvād iti cen, nânumiter api tadvad aprāmāṇya-prasaṅgāt. na ca viparītâkāra-nirākaraṇa-caturatayânumitir viśeṣavatī, nirṇīter api tad-apanoda-dakṣatvād, asamāropa-viṣaye 'pravṛtteḥ. tri-rūpa-liṅga-jatayā viśeṣo 'numiter mānatā-sādhaka iti cet, sākṣād anubhavād utpādas tarhi nirṇīter mahâparādha iti bhavato bālatām īkṣāmahe. kiṃ ca, yathā nirvikalpakam alakṣitaṃ sakala-vyāvṛtta-svalakṣaṇa-grahaṇa-pravaṇam api katicid-aṃśa-viṣayaṃ vikalpam utthāpayati, tathârtha evêndriyâlokâdi-sannikṛṣṭatayā katicin-nijâṃśa-viṣayaṃ sākṣād-viśada-vikalpaṃ janayed iti kim ajā-gala-stana-kalpa-nirvikalpaka-kalpanayā? tāvanto 'ṃśā bahir-arthe virudhyanta iti cet, pāṭavâpāṭavâdayo darśane 'py ekasmin na virudhyanta iti kiṃ rājñām ājñā? tasmān na kṣaṇa-kṣayi-paramâṇu-lakṣaṇa-svalakṣaṇa-lakṣakaṃ kvacit kadācid darśanaṃ lakṣayanti bhavanto 'pi, kevalaṃ sva-darśanânuraktântaḥ-karaṇatayā na tad-asattāṃ pratipadyante. svâṃśa-vyāpinaṃ kālântarânuyāyinam ekaṃ bahir antaś cârthaṃ bodhaṃ ca prakāśayan prathamāno nirṇayaḥ, na punar nirmūlakaiḥ kuyukti-vikalpair bādhyata iti na bhrāntaḥ. kiṃ câsya bhrāntatāṃ kathayan sarva-pramāṇa-prameya-vyavasthām unmūlyati. tathā hi: yat sattva-bodha-rūpatva-sukhatvâdiṣu pramāṇaṃ tad eva kṣaṇa-kṣayitva-svarga-prāpaṇa-śakti-yuktatvâdiṣv apramāṇam; tathā yad vastu nīla-caturasrôrdhvatâdi-rūpatayā prameyaṃ tad eva madhya-bhāga-kṣaṇa-vivartâdinâprameyaṃ; tathā yad bahir-arthâpekṣayā savikalpakaṃ svapnâdi-darśanaṃ vā bhrāntaṃ tad eva svarūpâpekṣayâbhrāntam; tathā yan niśīthinī-nātha-dvayâdikaṃ dvitve 'līkaṃ tad api dhavalatā-niyata-deśa-cāritâdāv analīkam iti nirṇayaḥ. yadi tu virodhād bibhyadbhir bhavadbhir ayam apahnūyate, kim aparam aikāntikaṃ pramāṇaṃ prameyaṃ côrarī-kṛtya svâkūtaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyur iti sakautukaṃ naś cetaḥ.
children.translated_text: [say that] the appearance of <s>anekānta</s> is unestablished because of the absence of everything — no, because even for them, in the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge), there is no awareness of the absence of everything; otherwise, even the opponent who says 'everything exists everywhere without valid means of knowledge' would suffer no defeat in his assertion, and upon accepting that [total absence], the acceptance itself would be impaired. And since both [<s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s>] display the appearance of <s>anekānta</s> as has been shown — the reason is not unestablished. Do not suspect that this [reason] is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) because even in a cognition that touches upon a mirage in the desert, where there is a mere trace of water, there is no acceptance of that [water] as its object-domain — because that [cognition] is erroneous; for it is the non-erroneous appearance that is the reason for accepting [something as an] object-domain. Now if you were to say that even this [<s>anekānta</s>-appearance] is erroneous because it is sublated by a cognition of mutually negated atoms perishing in an instant — that is untenable. For is that cognition mere apprehension, or is it a determination? If the first alternative, then inference would be destroyed, because it would be without an object-domain, since by the very first, primary, indeterminate perception — out of fear of contradiction — the grasping of the thing in all respects would be accepted, and because another <s>pramāṇa</s> would be useless when [the object] is [already] grasped by [one] <s>pramāṇa</s>, and because an infinite regress would follow. If the second, then in that case all indeterminate perception (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) would become non-<s>pramāṇa</s>. Nor does determination sublate the appearance of <s>anekānta</s> — rather, it supports it, because both externally and internally it manifests in precisely that way. Now if you were to think that even though indeterminate perception grasps the thing in all respects, it attains the status of <s>pramāṇa</s> only with respect to those aspects where it generates a subsequent determination that produces practical activity, and not elsewhere — in that case, the very determination immediately after which a person engages in seeking an object capable of purposeful activity would assume validity, not the indeterminate perception; even though [indeterminate perception] is the cause of that [determination], it would be like contact (<s>sannikarṣa</s>) and the like — this objection would attach. If [you say] indeterminate perception is the <s>pramāṇa</s> because it apprehends a previously unapprehended object, and determination is not, because it is a conceptual construction — no, because there would be the absurd consequence that inference too would likewise become non-<s>pramāṇa</s>. Nor does inference have any special distinction through its skill in eliminating contrary forms, since determination too is capable of removing those [contraries], because it does not operate with respect to what is not superimposed. If [you say] the distinguishing feature of inference that establishes its validity is its arising from a mark possessing the three characteristics (<s>trirūpa-liṅga</s>) — then, since determination arises directly from experience, we perceive your childishness in considering that a great fault. Moreover, just as indeterminate perception, though unperceived and directed toward grasping <s>svalakṣaṇas</s> (own-characteristics) differentiated from everything [else], generates a determinate cognition pertaining to only some aspects — so too, the object itself, being in contact with the sense-organ, light, etc., should directly produce a vivid determinate cognition pertaining to only some of its own aspects — so what is the point of fabricating an indeterminate perception like the nipple on a goat's neck? If [you say] that many aspects are contradicted in the external object — [we reply that] degrees of clarity and the like are not contradicted even in a single perception, so what is this — the decree of kings? Therefore, you too never perceive any perception at any time that apprehends <s>svalakṣaṇas</s> characterized by atoms perishing in an instant; it is only because your inner faculties are enamored of your own system that you do not acknowledge its non-existence. Determination, manifesting as illuminating a single object — both external and internal, both awareness and its object — that pervades its own aspects and continues across time, is not sublated by baseless conceptual fabrications of bad reasoning — therefore it is not erroneous. Moreover, one who declares it erroneous uproots the entire structure of all <s>pramāṇas</s> and <s>prameyas</s>. For consider: the very [cognition] that is a <s>pramāṇa</s> with respect to existence, the nature of cognition, pleasantness, and the like is a non-<s>pramāṇa</s> with respect to momentariness, the power of leading to heaven, and the like; likewise, the very thing that is <s>prameya</s> (knowable) in the form of blue, square, tall, etc. is not <s>prameya</s> with respect to the middle portion, momentary transformation, etc.; likewise, the very determinate cognition or dream-perception that is erroneous with respect to external objects is non-erroneous with respect to its own nature; likewise, what is unreal as two moons, etc. in respect of duality, is not unreal in respect of whiteness, fixed location, behavior, etc. — such is the determination. But if you, fearing contradiction, deny this, we are curious to know: having embraced what other absolute <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> would you establish your own position?

children.text: advaita-prakāśam alakṣitam abhyupetya tena bāhuvidhyaṃ dadhāno bodho bādhyamānatvād bhrānta ity abhidadhyāt, tad ayuktam, dṛṣṭa-hāny-adṛṣṭa-parikalpanā-prasaṅgād, alakṣita-nirvikalpa-darśanasya ca prāg eva pratikṣiptatvāt. atha yuktir bodhasya vaividhyaṃ bādheta, tathā hi: bhrāntâbhrānta-saṃvedana-vivekasya kartum aśakyatvāt, saṃvin-mātrasya tu sarvatrâvyabhicāritvād, advayaṃ saṃvedanaṃ vivikta-yuktyā prakāśamānam anādi-kālâlīna-vāsanā-samupajanita-saṃvṛti-darśita-sattākaṃ sitâsitâdi-vividha-pratibhāsaṃ nirākurute. atra pratividadhmahe: kim ayam anekâkāro bodho 'dvaya-saṃvedanād vyatyaraikṣīd vā na vā. kiṃ câto, yadi vyabhaitsīt, katham adṛṣṭa-tat-kāryatve vyatirikto 'yaṃ tad advayaṃ saṃvedanam anumāpayet? avyatireka-pakṣe punar anekaḥ sann eka-saṃvedana-tādātmyena prathamānaḥ katham advaitaṃ nôddalayet? atha saṃvṛti-darśitatvād alīkatayâsya sitâsitâdy-ākāra-bahir-mukha-kāluṣyasya bodhena tāttvikena saha bhedâbheda-vikalpânupapattir iti brūṣe, tathā sati paro bodhasyâpāramārthikatvaṃ avidyā-darśitatvād, artha-sattāyāḥ punas tattva-rūpatā, sarvatrâvyabhicārād iti bruvāṇo durnivāraḥ syāt. jaḍasya prakāśâyogāt saṃvittiḥ satyā, nârtha iti ced, ekasyânekatâvabhāsâbhāvād anekântaḥ satyo, nâdvaitam iti pratijānīmahe. saṃvṛtyâdvayasyâpi nānā-pratibhāso 'viruddha iti ced, anādy-avidyā-balāj jaḍasyâpi cetanatayā prakāśo na viruddha iti parasyâpi śaṭhôttaraṃ nâtidurlabhaṃ bhavet. kiṃ ca, nānâkāra-kaluṣita-caitanya-sāmānyasyânyathânupapatti-sāmarthyatas tasya siddhatvād advayaṃ saṃvedanam asiddhaṃ sādhayed ayam, anyathā nirnibandhanatayā sādhanasyâpravṛttes, tathā ca sthira-sthūrâdy-upalakṣitârthâṃśa-vaśād viśakalita-paramâṇu-kṣaṇa-kṣayi-paryāya-tādātmyaṃ sādhayan tam anekânta-vādinaṃ na pratikṣeptum arhati, yukter ubhayatrâpi tulyatvāt. kiṃ ca, yo 'yaṃ sita-pītâdy-anekâkāra-nirṇayo 'sāv api sva-saṃvedanâpekṣayâdvaya-rūpa iti bhavad-abhiprāyo; yathā cânavasthā-bhīrutayā sarvaṃ jñānaṃ sva-prakāśam abhyupetaṃ, tathā sarvo niścayaḥ sva-niścāyako 'bhyupagantavyo, 'nyathā tatrâpy anavasthā-doṣo 'nuṣajyeta, niścayāś ca sarvathā svarūpaṃ niścinuyur, nâika-deśena, yato "niścayair yan na niścīyate rūpaṃ tat teṣāṃ viṣayaḥ katham" iti svayam eva sva-vadhāya pralapitam. tathā câdvayasya kṣaṇa-kṣayiṇaḥ svarūpasya tair grahaṇe viparītâropâbhāvād ādita eva anutthānaṃ saṃsārasyêti yukti-rikta evâmuktatâbhimānaḥ syāt, na câivam, bhava-bhāvasya pratiprāṇi-prasiddhatvāt. tan nâyam itarêtarâvinirluṭhita-dravya-paryāya-prakāśo bhrāntas, tad-viparītârthôpasthāpaka-pramāṇântarâbhāvād iti sthitam.
children.translated_text: having accepted the unperceived appearance of non-dual [awareness], were to say that cognition, bearing multiplicity by virtue of that [non-dual awareness], is erroneous because it is sublated — that is untenable, because of the absurd consequence of abandoning the observed and fabricating the unobserved, and because the unperceived indeterminate perception has already been rejected earlier. Now, if [you say that] reasoning sublates the multiplicity of cognition — for consider: since the discrimination between erroneous and non-erroneous awareness is impossible to make, and since awareness-in-general is invariable everywhere, the non-dual awareness, manifesting through discriminating reasoning, refutes the variegated appearance of white, dark, etc., the existence of which is displayed by the conventional perspective (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) generated by beginningless latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) — to this we reply: Does this manifold cognition differ from non-dual awareness or not? What of it? If it did differ, how could this [manifold cognition], being distinct and having no observed effect of that [non-dual awareness], serve as a means of inferring that non-dual awareness? In the position of non-difference, on the other hand, being manifold and yet manifesting through identity with unitary awareness, how would it not shatter non-duality? Now if you say that because [the manifold appearance] is shown from the conventional perspective, this impurity of outward-facing forms such as white, dark, etc., being unreal, admits of neither the conceptual alternative of difference nor non-difference with real cognition — in that case, the opponent who says that cognition is non-ultimate because it is shown by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), while the existence of objects has the nature of reality because it is invariable everywhere — he would be impossible to refute. If [you say] that consciousness is real because what is inert cannot be illuminated, while objects are not [real] — [we reply:] since <s>anekānta</s> (many-sidedness) is real because the appearance of multiplicity in a unitary [entity] is not absent, while non-duality is not — thus we maintain. If [you say] even for the non-dual, manifold appearance is not contradicted by the conventional [perspective] — then [we reply:] the opponent too, for whom even the inert appears as conscious by the power of beginningless <s>avidyā</s>, would not find a clever rejoinder very difficult to obtain. Moreover, since cognition-in-general, tinged with manifold forms, is established through the force of the reasoning of 'no-other-explanation-possible' (<s>anyathānupapatti</s>), this [reason] would be proving what is unestablished — namely non-dual awareness — since otherwise, the proof would not proceed due to its being without foundation. And thus, [the <s>Yogācāra</s>], in proving through the force of aspects pertaining to objects characterized as stable, gross, etc. the identity with modes characterized by atoms perishing in an instant that have been analytically separated — should not reject the proponent of <s>anekānta</s>, since the reasoning is equal in both cases. Moreover, this determination of many forms such as white, yellow, etc. — that too, from the perspective of <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness), has a non-dual nature — such is your position. And just as, out of fear of an infinite regress, all knowledge is accepted as self-luminous, so too all determination must be accepted as self-determining; otherwise the fault of infinite regress would attach there too. And determinations would determine their own nature in all respects, not partially — because 'that form which is not determined by determinations, how can it be their object-domain?' — this is something you yourselves have blurted out to your own destruction. And thus, if the non-dual, momentarily-perishing own-nature is grasped by those [determinations], since there would be no superimposition of the opposite from the very beginning, <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) would never have arisen — so the conceit of being unliberated would be merely an empty reasoning exercise. But this is not so, because the existence of worldly life is well-known to every living being. Therefore, this appearance that illuminates <s>dravya</s> (substance) and <s>paryāya</s> (mode) without mutual negation is not erroneous, because there is no other <s>pramāṇa</s> that presents a contrary meaning — this is established.

children.text: ‘nirālambanāḥ sarve pratyayāḥ, pratyayatvāt, svapna-pratyayavad'; iti parâbhiprāya-pravṛttânumāna-balād bhrāntatām asya kathayet, tadā taṃ prati ‘sâlambanāḥ sarve pratyayāḥ, pratyayatvāj, jāgrad-daśā-pratyayavad'; iti viparītânumānam upaḍhaukanīyam. sa yadi dṛṣṭântasya sādhya-vikalatām udbhāvayet, tadā tad-dṛṣṭânte 'pi sā darśanīyā. yadi punar asau svapna-pratyayasya nirālambanatvaṃ bhavadbhir abhipretam iti vilapann āsituṃ na dadyāt, tadā sa vikalpataḥ paryanuyojyo: 'smad-abhyupagamaḥ pramāṇaṃ bhavato 'pramāṇaṃ vā? pramāṇaṃ ced, yathā tad-balād dṛṣṭânta-samarthanaṃ tathā jāgrat-pratyaya-gocarârtha-samarthanam api kiṃ na kuruṣe, ko 'yam ardha-jaratīya-nyāyaḥ? athâpramāṇam, evaṃ sati svapna-pratyaya-nirālambanatā-sādhakaṃ pramāṇântaraṃ mṛgaṇīyaṃ, kim anena kuśa-kāśâvalambanena. tatrâpi pramāṇântare vikalpa-yugalam amalam avatarati: tat kiṃ nirālambanaṃ sâlambanaṃ vā? nirālambanaṃ cen, nânya-pratyayasya nirālambanatāṃ gadituṃ paṭiṣṭhaṃ, nirgocaratvāt. atha sâlambanaṃ, hanta hato 'si, nirālambanāḥ sarve pratyayā iti pratijñāta-kṣater, anenâiva vyabhicārād iti śaṭhaḥ pratiśaṭhâcaraṇena nirloṭhanīyaḥ. tan nâsyânaikāntikatvam.
children.translated_text: would declare this [<s>anekānta</s>-appearance] erroneous by the force of inference directed at the opponent's position — [namely] 'all cognitions are without a real support (<s>nirālambana</s>), because they are cognitions, like dream-cognitions' — then against him, the counter-inference should be offered: 'all cognitions have a real support (<s>sālambana</s>), because they are cognitions, like waking-state cognitions.' If he should raise the deficiency of the example with respect to the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved), then that same [deficiency] should be shown in his example too. If, however, he will not allow [the discussion] to rest, complaining that 'the supportlessness of dream-cognition is what is intended by you [Jains]' — then he should be pressed with a dilemma: 'Is our acceptance a <s>pramāṇa</s> for you, or a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>? If a <s>pramāṇa</s>, then just as by its force you support your example, why do you not also thereby support the reality of the object-domain of waking cognitions — what is this logic of the half-old-woman? If a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>, then in that case, another <s>pramāṇa</s> establishing the supportlessness of dream-cognition must be sought — what is the use of grasping at straws? Even regarding that other <s>pramāṇa</s>, a pure pair of alternatives descends: Is it without a support or with a support? If without a support, it is not fit to declare the supportlessness of another cognition, because it has no object-domain. If with a support — well then, you are defeated, since the thesis that all cognitions are without support is impaired, because this very [<s>pramāṇa</s>] constitutes a counter-example.' Thus the rogue should be dealt with by counter-roguery. Therefore there is no inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntika</s>) of this [reason].

children.text: viruddhatā-śaṅkā punar dūrâpāsta-prasarâiva, pramāṇa-prakāśite 'rthe sarva-vādināṃ tathâbhyupagamâvigānād iti. anena saṃśaya-virodhânavasthā-vaiyadhikaraṇyâsambhavâdi-dūṣaṇāni nirmūlaka-mithyā-vikalpôtthāpitāni pratibhāsa-mudgara-nipāta-nirdalita-mastakatvān na jīvitum utsahanta iti. tasmād asiddhatâdi-doṣa-vinā-kṛto 'yaṃ tathā-pratibhāsa-lakṣaṇo hetur anekânta-gocaratāṃ pramāṇasya parān abhyupagamayatîty alam vistareṇa. tasmāt ‘tasyâiva tatra pratibhāsanāt';
children.translated_text: The suspicion of contradiction (<s>viruddhatā</s>) is itself utterly devoid of scope, because when an object is illuminated by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, all disputants accept it in just that way without dispute. By this [argument], the objections of doubt, contradiction, infinite regress, mutual exclusion of loci (<s>vaiyadhikaraṇya</s>), impossibility, and so forth — raised by baseless false conceptual fabrications — because their heads are shattered by the blow of the club of [direct] appearance, do not manage to survive. Therefore this reason, characterized by such appearance and free from the faults of unestablishedness and the like, compels others to accept that the object-domain of <s>pramāṇa</s> is <s>anekānta</s> (many-sided) — enough with prolixity. Therefore, 'because it is precisely that which appears therein';
the object-domain of all cognitions is a thing whose nature is <s>anekānta</s> (many-sided)

children.text: ayaṃ ca yathâvasthita-pramāṇa-vyāpāra-paryālocaka-pramātr-abhiprāyeṇa pramāṇa-gocaro darśitaḥ. nayas tarhi kiṃ-bhūtam taṃ manyata iti vacanâvakāśe saty āha:
children.translated_text: And this object-domain of <s>pramāṇa</s> has been shown from the perspective of the knower who reflects upon the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> as it actually is. Now, what does <s>naya</s> (standpoint) consider it to be? — when there is occasion for [this] statement, he says:

children.text: ty-ādi. ananta-dharmâdhyāsitaṃ vastu svâbhipretâika-dharma-viśiṣṭaṃ nayati prāpayati saṃvedanam ārohayatîti
children.translated_text: and so forth. A thing invested with infinite properties — [<s>naya</s>] leads, i.e., brings, i.e., causes awareness to ascend to [that thing as] qualified by one particular property that it intends — thus it is

children.text: , pramāṇa-pravṛtter uttara-kāla-bhāvī parāmarśa ity arthas; tasya
children.translated_text: meaning a consideration that occurs after the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s>; its
characterized by a property such as permanence, etc.;

children.text: prameya-rūpaṃ, pramāṇam evaṃ-vidham evârthaṃ gṛhṇātîti svâkutena tena vyavasthāpanād iti.
children.translated_text: means the <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge); because <s>pramāṇa</s> grasps precisely such an object, [the <s>naya</s>] establishes it according to its own intention.

children.text: athavā pramāṇa-viṣayāṃ lakṣaṇa-saṃkhyā-gocara-phala-rūpāṃ catur-vidhāṃ vipratipattiṃ nirākṛtyâtrâiva naya-gocaraṃ nirūpayann āha:
children.translated_text: Alternatively, having refuted the fourfold disagreement pertaining to the domain of <s>pramāṇa</s> — consisting of definition, enumeration, object-domain, and result — he now, while determining the object-domain of <s>naya</s> in this very [context], says:

children.text: ty-ādi. nanu câdi-vākyena pramāṇa-vyutpādana-mātraṃ pratijñānaṃ, tat kiṃ ayam aprastuto 'tra naya-gocaraḥ pratipādyata iti. satyaṃ, evaṃ manyate: na nayaḥ pramāṇād atyantaṃ dūra-yāyī, kiṃ tarhi tad-aṃśa-bhūta eva, naya-samudāya-sampādyatvāt pramāṇasyâtas tad-vyutpādana-pratijñāne 'sāv api ‘tan-madhya-patitas tad-grahaṇena gṛhyata'; iti-nyāyād gṛhīta eva, tan nâyam aprastuta iti.
children.translated_text: and so forth. Objection: since the opening statement promised only the exposition of <s>pramāṇa</s>, why is this unrelated topic of the object-domain of <s>naya</s> being expounded here? True, [but] the view is this: <s>naya</s> does not travel exceedingly far from <s>pramāṇa</s>; rather, it is a constituent part of it, because <s>pramāṇa</s> is accomplished through the assemblage of <s>nayas</s>. Therefore, in the promise to expound <s>pramāṇa</s>, that [<s>naya</s>] too, falling within it, is grasped by the grasping of that [<s>pramāṇa</s>] — according to the maxim [that what falls within the scope of a term is included by that term]. Therefore this is not an unrelated topic.

children.text: atrâpi padârthaḥ sa eva, kevalaṃ vākyârtha-bhedaḥ. tathā hîhâivaṃ ghaṭanā:
children.translated_text: Here too the word-meaning is the same; only the sentence-meaning differs. For here the construction is thus:
the domain of <s>naya</s> is an object qualified by one aspect — [this is] considered

children.text: nītividām iti. nanu ca yadi nayasya pramāṇântaḥ-pātitve 'pi pṛthag gocaraḥ pratipādyate, tataḥ pramāṇavad etad-viṣayā lakṣaṇâdi-vipratipattir api nirākartavyā. satyaṃ, kiṃ tu na pareṣāṃ naya-vyavahāraḥ prasiddho, 'to dharmiṇo 'bhāvāt tad-gocarā vipratipattir nâsty eva. na ca te tena tattvaṃ pratipādanīyās, tattva-pratipādane pramāṇasyâiva vyāpārān, nayasya punar eka-deśa-niṣṭhatvena tat-pratipādana-sāmarthya-vikalatvād, ata evâcāryasya na tal-lakṣaṇâdi-svarūpa-kathane 'pi mahânādaraḥ. gocaraṃ punar heya-pakṣe kākvā prakṣipan sākṣāt pratipādayati: mā bhūt sva-darśanântaḥ-pātināṃ manda-buddhīnāṃ pramāṇa-pratipanne 'py anekântâtmake vastuny eka-deśa-samarthanâbhiniveśa-lakṣaṇaḥ kadāgraha iti. athavā sva-darśanântaḥ-pātinaḥ praty anenâiva gocara-kathanenôpalakṣaṇatvāl lakṣaṇâdīny api lakṣayati. tatra pramāṇa-pratipannârthâika-deśa-parāmarśo naya iti lakṣaṇaṃ, sarva-naya-viśeṣânuyāyitvāt para-rūpa-vyāvartana-kṣamatvāc câsya. saṃkhyayā punar anantā iti, ananta-dharmatvād vastunas, tad-eka-dharma-paryavasitâbhiprāyāṇāṃ ca nayatvāt, tathâpi cirantanâcāryaiḥ sarva-saṅgrāhi-saptâbhiprāya-parikalpanā-dvāreṇa sapta nayāḥ pratipāditāḥ. tad yathā -- ‘naigama-saṅgraha-vyavahāra-rjusūtra-śabda-samabhirūḍhâivambhūtā nayā'; iti. ato 'smābhir api ta eva varṇyante.
children.translated_text: by those versed in [philosophical] viewpoints. Objection: if, even though <s>naya</s> falls within the scope of <s>pramāṇa</s>, its separate object-domain is being expounded, then the disagreement regarding definition and the like pertaining to its domain should also be refuted, as was done for <s>pramāṇa</s>. True, but opponents do not have the well-known practice of <s>naya</s>; therefore, since the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) is absent, there is simply no disagreement regarding its domain. Nor should they be instructed in reality through it [<s>naya</s>], since the exposition of reality is the function of <s>pramāṇa</s> alone, and since <s>naya</s>, being confined to one aspect, lacks the capacity to expound that [reality]. For this very reason, the master [<s>Siddhasena</s>] does not have great regard even for stating its definition and the like. The object-domain, however, he expounds directly, casting [it] into the category of what is to be rejected by [his] tone of voice — [thinking:] let there not be, among those of dull intellect who fall within our own school, the obstinate attachment characterized by insistence on establishing one aspect alone, even when the thing has been established by <s>pramāṇa</s> as having the nature of <s>anekānta</s>. Alternatively, by this very statement of the object-domain, since it serves as an indicator, he also indicates the definition and the like for those who fall within his own school. There, the definition is: <s>naya</s> is the consideration of one aspect of a thing established by <s>pramāṇa</s> — because this [definition] follows all particular <s>nayas</s> and is capable of distinguishing [<s>naya</s>] from what is of a different kind. In enumeration, moreover, they are infinite — because things have infinite properties, and because the viewpoints of those whose intentions are confined to one particular property of a thing are [correspondingly many]. Nevertheless, the ancient masters, through the device of constructing seven all-encompassing categories of intention, have expounded seven <s>nayas</s>. They are as follows: '<s>Naigama</s> (figurative), <s>Saṅgraha</s> (synthetic), <s>Vyavahāra</s> (practical), <s>Ṛjusūtra</s> (straight-thread), <s>Śabda</s> (verbal), <s>Samabhirūḍha</s> (etymological), and <s>Evambhūta</s> (such-like) — [these are] the <s>nayas</s>.' Therefore we too shall describe those very [seven].
